add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.prTitle: Add AuthzClientCryptoProvider for authorization client cryptographic operations

prOriginal.nota: Found by gh search on 'AuthzClientCryptoProvider'. Single PR commit is the benchmark head 79d11c48; squash commit b95d12a9 on main touches the same 12 files with the same line counts. Backported to release/26.0 as #34003.

add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.bug: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.reason: CryptoProvider.java on main still declares `int order();` with no default, and CryptoIntegration.detectProvider still sorts every ServiceLoader provider with Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order). Later commits to CryptoProvider (#43432 import order, RSA 3072, BCFKS truststore) did not add a default.
add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.reasonUpstreamV4: keycloak/keycloak main (read 2026-11-13) still declares `int order();` without a default in CryptoProvider, and CryptoIntegration.detectProvider still sorts with Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order). Commits since 2024-10-15 (c7cc162f, a2c1055f #43432, 1c8445f9 #50149) did not touch it.

evidenciaV4.opus: Astra's input needs a separately compiled CryptoProvider binary without order(), loaded next to head keycloak-common. No such binary exists in a supported setup. Every CryptoProvider in the repo (AuthzClientCryptoProvider, DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, WildFlyElytronProvider) implements order() in this PR and ships at the same version as keycloak-common. CryptoProvider is an internal fips/non-fips abstraction, not a documented third-party SPI, so the input is a mixed-version classpath, not a realistic one. The comparison at CryptoIntegration.java:56 does reach order() when there are two providers. But the only providers on the classpath are Keycloak's own same-version jars, so no AbstractMethodError occurs.
evidenciaV4.astra: Changing to FP. The PR adds order() to every concrete provider implementation in the repository; the strict FIPS provider inherits it. My earlier example required a separately compiled legacy provider mixed with newer Keycloak artifacts, without establishing a real caller that supplies that combination. The possible linkage error therefore does not meet the required reachability standard.

add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.bug: detectProvider no longer fails when several crypto providers are present; with Default, FIPS and Elytron all at order 200, ties are resolved by classpath order and a FIPS deployment can silently run with the non-FIPS provider.
add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.reason: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider on main is unchanged: sorts by order() and returns the first, only logging ignored providers, with no tie/multiple-provider error. DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider and WildFlyElytronProvider all still return 200 from order().
add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.reasonUpstreamV4: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider on main is unchanged since the merge apart from import reordering (a2c1055f #43432): it sorts by order() and returns get(0), only logging the ignored providers. Default, FIPS and Elytron still return 200.

evidenciaV4.opus: [desk] input: keycloak-crypto-default and keycloak-crypto-fips1402 both visible to the ClassLoader passed to CryptoIntegration.init. | observed: Tracing each production entry point. (1) Quarkus server: quarkus/runtime/pom.xml:175-179 ships both jars, but KeycloakRecorder.java:210-215 calls CryptoIntegration.setProvider(fipsMode.getProviderClassName()), so detectProvider never runs. CryptoIntegration.java:30-33 init is a no-op once a provider is set. (2) kcadm/kcreg: client-cli-dist ships both jars, but ClassLoaderUtil.resolveClassLoader puts only keycloak-crypto-fips1402 + bc-fips OR keycloak-crypto-default + bcprov on the URLClassLoader passed to Globals.java:44, never both. (3) authz-client: authz/client/pom.xml does not depend on any keycloak-crypto-* jar, so normally only AuthzClientCryptoProvider (100) is present, plus whatever single provider the user adds, which wins as intended. | expected: An error (or a deterministic choice) when two equal-order providers are present. | The tie at CryptoIntegration.java:57/71 only matters when two order-200 providers are on one classloader. None of Keycloak's callers builds such a classloader (KeycloakRecorder.java:214 bypasses detection; ClassLoaderUtil filters to a single crypto jar). The remaining case is a user app that puts both default and FIPS jars on its classpath. That is a misconfiguration, and losing the fail-fast check for it is hardening, not a reachable defect. When in doubt, FP.

add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.bug: The ES384 and ES512 tests sign with the same default P-256 key, so the converter is never tested with real P-384 or P-521 signatures.
add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.reason: ECDSAAlgorithmTest on main still builds one KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() (default curve) in the constructor and reuses it for ES256/ES384/ES512. Only change after merge was the import-order commit #43432.
add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.reasonUpstreamV4: ECDSAAlgorithmTest on main still builds a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() in the constructor and reuses it for ES256/ES384/ES512. The only later commit is import ordering a2c1055f (#43432).

evidenciaV4.opus: Astra's premise that the default key is P-256 doesn't hold on current JDKs. On eclipse-temurin:21, KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") at ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:42 yields a 384-bit key for all three tests (ev/3/output.txt: keyCurveBits=384). So testES512 never sees a P-521 signature. The >127-byte DER long-form length path of ASN1Encoder is never used (encoderLongFormLengthPathUsed=false). Only a real secp521r1 key reaches it (jdkDerLen=139, long form=true). This is a test-quality defect: the test named for ES512 doesn't verify the ES512 behaviour it was written for. Under RUBRICA that counts without a separate production misconversion.
evidenciaV4.astra: Changing to TP (category: test_gap). ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates its key without selecting a curve; changing the signature algorithm and output width does not change that key’s curve. Consequently, the ES512 case using the reported P-384 default never exercises actual P-521 components or the DER sequence’s long-form length encoding. The exact default is JDK-dependent, but the substantive coverage defect exists, and the rubric does not require a separate production failure.

add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.bug: The test only checks a round trip between the two new converters and never verifies the re-encoded DER against the original signature or with Signature.verify, so mutually consistent bugs go undetected.
add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.reason: ECDSAAlgorithmTest.test on main still asserts only assertArrayEquals(rsConcat, rsConcat2) after a decode/encode/decode round trip, never comparing asn1Des to the original signature nor calling Signature.verify.
add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.reasonUpstreamV4: ECDSAAlgorithmTest.test on main still ends with Assert.assertArrayEquals(rsConcat, rsConcat2) after decode/encode/decode. It never compares asn1Des with the original signature and never calls Signature.verify. Only later change: import ordering (#43432).

evidenciaV4.opus: Astra says no input was shown where this assertion accepts an incorrect signature. ev/4 shows one: the unmodified test runs on JDK 21 with a default P-384 key. In testES256, AuthzClientCryptoProvider.integerToBytes truncates the 48-byte r/s to 32 bytes. The re-encoded DER doesn't equal the original and fails Signature.verify (asn1DesEqualsOriginal=false, asn1DesVerifies=false), yet testAssertion=PASS. The assertion at ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:53-56 only checks that a lossy, idempotent conversion is self-consistent. So the test passes while the converter emits a non-verifying signature, which shows it doesn't verify converter correctness.
evidenciaV4.astra: Changing to TP (category: test_gap). Lines 53–56 compare two concatenated representations only after the first conversion has potentially lost information. The reported P-384-key/ES256 case follows the code: integerToBytes retains only 32 bytes per component, and subsequent conversions preserve those truncated values, allowing the assertion to pass despite a corrupted signature. Comparing the reconstructed DER with the original or verifying it would detect this actual failure; my earlier requirement for a hypothetical converter mutation was incorrect.

add-caching-support-for-identityprovider.bug: On a partial cache miss getForLogin merges the previously read login query into a newly revisioned entry, so a concurrent invalidation can be lost and stale IDP IDs for other organizations persist.
add-caching-support-for-identityprovider.reason: Today getForLogin on main still does, on a partial miss, cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey); loaded = cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey); new IdentityProviderListQuery(loaded, ..., cached, query); cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()), and IdentityProviderListQuery's second constructor still copies previous.searchKeys without validation. File history since the merge (ordering, imports, multi-org ids) never touched this merge logic.
add-caching-support-for-identityprovider.reasonUpstreamV4: On main (read 2026-11-13) getForLogin's partial-miss branch still does invalidateObject; getCurrentRevision; new IdentityProviderListQuery(loaded, ..., cached, query); addRevisioned(query, getCurrentCounter()), and the second IdentityProviderListQuery constructor still copies previous.searchKeys unvalidated. Commits since 2024-09-18 (incl. 932cee4307 2026-09-02, 90b3f7e6fa 2026-10-30) did not touch this logic.

Saying a hypothetical broken merge would escape the test describes incomplete coverage, not an existing defect or an ineffective test, so under 'when in doubt, FP' this is FP.
evidenciaV4.astra: I keep FP (no subclass). The test never reaches the merge branch, but the head constructs a replacement query that copies previous.searchKeys before adding the new organization’s results. The test meaningfully verifies cache population and invalidation, including changed counts after updates. Showing that a hypothetical broken merge would escape those assertions establishes incomplete coverage, not an existing defect or a test that fails to verify its stated scenario.

add-caching-support-for-identityprovider.bug: getLoginPredicate treats BROKER_PUBLIC case-insensitively, but the JPA delegate matches the exact value "true". An update that only changes the case (e.g. true -> TRUE) skips login-cache invalidation, so the cached login IDP list no longer matches the delegate.
add-caching-support-for-identityprovider.reasonUpstreamV4: Two days after the merge, PR #32668 'Remove the kc.org.broker.public attribute and use hideOnLogin in the IDP instead' deleted the Boolean.parseBoolean(BROKER_PUBLIC) clause from LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate and the searchOptions.put(BROKER_PUBLIC, "true") from getForLogin, replacing the mechanism with hideOnLogin; it targeted the attribute's removal, not this case mismatch.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.prTitle: Add Client resource type and scopes to authorization schema

prOriginal.nota: Found via gh pr list search on the title (branch 35564-client-authz-schema). Its single commit is the benchmark head 1950a511026d; merged as 7e5540896b (rebase), so merged code equals the benchmark head. Files later moved to admin/fgap/ and authorization/fgap/ (May 2025).

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: The V1-only guard in AdminPermissions.registerListener is still there today (now in admin/fgap/AdminPermissions.java), but V2 cleanup was added separately: PR #37984 'Remove permissions and resources when their corresponding objects are deleted' (closes #37242) added AdminPermissionsSchema.removeResourceObject, called from ClientApplicationSynchronizer/GroupSynchronizer/RoleSynchronizer/UserSynchronizer on ClientRemovedEvent etc., gated on V2 being enabled. So under V2 the per-object resources and permissions are no longer orphaned.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #38015 'Fix permissions for view-members and manage-members' (commit b200ab0792) replaced resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) with policyStore.findByResourceType(...) flattened to policy.getResources(), so the method returns the names (client ids) of the per-client resources referenced by permissions instead of the type-level 'Clients' resource. It was later renamed getClientIdsByScope and today delegates to FineGrainedAdminPermissionEvaluator.getIdsByScope with the same policy-based logic.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: The findByResource call was rewritten in April 2025 (9f079f7874, then moved into FineGrainedAdminPermissionEvaluator), but a null from getResourceTypeResource still dereferenced (resourceTypeResource.getScopes()). Issue #43331 reported exactly this NPE (500 after disabling realm admin permissions), and PR #43353 'Check FGAP enabled before proceeding with evaluation' added `if (!AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.isAdminPermissionsEnabled(root.realm)) return false;` before the lookup, closing the reachable null case.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: canView() still checks only VIEW today, and PR #38559 (2025-04-02) made that deliberate by removing MANAGE->VIEW transitiveness everywhere. The slow path itself was removed by PR #38396 'Support for partial evaluation for clients': ClientsResource now sets canView = isAdminPermissionsEnabled(realm) || auth.clients().canView(), so under FGAP V2 listing always uses the paginated store query with permission filtering pushed into the store.

astra.pergunta: #09: PR #38396 makes ClientsResource use the paginated store query whenever FGAP V2 is enabled (canView = isAdminPermissionsEnabled(realm) || canView()), and PR #38559 later removed MANAGE->VIEW transitiveness. Confirmado, pendente or descontinuado?
astra.resposta: Confirmado via PR #38396: under FGAP V2 the listing uses the paginated store query with partial evaluation, eliminating the slow path for global-MANAGE-only admins.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #38559 '[FGAP] remove transitiveness from auth scopes' replaced `if (canView() || canConfigure(client)) return true;` in canView(ClientModel) with an admin-role check followed by hasPermission(client, VIEW). Today canView(client) calls eval.hasPermission(new ClientModelRecord(client), null, VIEW), which evaluates the client's own resource (both specific and all-clients permissions apply) and grants only on a permission for that resource id; ClientsResource listing filters via partial evaluation (PR #38396).

astra.pergunta: #10: PR #38559 replaced `if (canView() || canConfigure(client)) return true` with an admin-role check followed by hasPermission(client, VIEW); today the evaluator evaluates the client's own resource with its resource type. Is the short-circuit bug fixed?
astra.resposta: Confirmado via PR #38559: removing the canView() shortcut forces VIEW evaluation on the specific client, and today's evaluator keeps applying both specific and all-clients permissions to that resource.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: The test was renamed ClientResourceTypeEvaluationTest and the weak block (getDefaultClientScopes() and removeDefaultClientScope in one try before any grant) is still there unchanged. But PR #50780 ([CVE-2026-14614] FGAP bypass in client scope assignment) added assertions that fetch the scopes with the full realm admin and call removeDefaultClientScope alone expecting Forbidden, plus testClientScopeAssignmentRequiresManageClientScopes, so the removal permission check is now actually exercised.

astra.pergunta: #11: the weak block (getDefaultClientScopes() then removeDefaultClientScope in one try) is still in testManageOnlyOneClient, but PR #50780 added removal assertions that fetch scopes via the full admin and isolate the remove call, plus testClientScopeAssignmentRequiresManageClientScopes. Confirmado or pendente?
astra.resposta: Confirmado via PR #50780: the new assertions isolate the removal call and close the coverage gap; the weak block remaining does not make it pendente.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #46967 'Fix deny unsupported FGAPv2 token-exchange audience checks' (closes #46718) changed ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo from throwing UnsupportedOperationException to `return false`, explicitly because V1 token exchange audience validation failed with HTTP 500 under FGAP V2. Main today still returns false.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: Commit 78aa8b486f ('User not visible when permission with different scope exists', closes #38369, in PR #38443 merged 2025-03-27) passed the resource type into ResourcePermission from ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission and made FGAPPolicyEvaluator.evaluateResourceTypePolicies also evaluate the policies of the all-clients type resource when a per-client resource is evaluated. It added ClientResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testEvaluateAllResourcePermissionsForSpecificResourcePermission, which asserts that the all-clients grant still applies once a per-client permission exists. Today's main (fgap/FGAPPolicyEvaluator + FineGrainedAdminPermissionEvaluator) keeps this behaviour.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName handles only USERS, so for the new CLIENTS resource type the admin API returns a null/UUID display name instead of 'All clients' or the clientId.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: At the merge, getResourceName(session, policy, resource) special-cased only USERS and fell back to resource.getDisplayName(). PR #37606 (commit 77ef5ff795) rewrote it to delegate to a new getResourceName(session, resourceServer, resourceType, resourceName) with a switch whose CLIENTS case returns the client's clientId (or the type name 'Clients' for the all-clients resource). Today's main (fgap/AdminPermissionsSchema.java) keeps that CLIENTS case and PolicyResourceService still uses it for displayName.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel) chains canView(), canManage(client), canConfigure(client) and the VIEW check, so one client can cost up to four full policy evaluations of the same resource. ClientsResource.getClients repeats this for every client in the listing.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reasonUpstreamV4: PR #38559 ("[FGAP] remove transitiveness from auth scopes") replaced canView(ClientModel)'s chain `canView() || canConfigure(client)` + hasPermission(VIEW) with an admin-role check plus a single VIEW evaluation. Today's main (admin/fgap/ClientPermissionsV2.java) does one eval.hasPermission(..., VIEW) per client. The chain was removed for semantic reasons, not for performance.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants role-mapping scopes on myclient and only exercises myclient, without checking that a second client stays forbidden. A regression that applies a per-client grant to all clients would still pass.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reasonUpstreamV4: PR #38639 (2025-04-07) split the test into testMapRolesOnlyOneClient and testMapCompositesToAnotherClientRole (now in ClientResourceTypeEvaluationTest). testMapRolesOnlyOneClient on main still grants MAP_ROLES on myclient and only exercises myclient, with no negative check on another client.

evidenciaV4.opus: Astra agrees the negative assertion is missing; the disagreement is only whether a test gap needs a production failure at head, and RUBRICA.md lists 'a test that does not verify the behaviour it was written for' as a real defect, so the input to show is the regression the test should catch, not a broken head. PermissionClientTest.java:326-365 is named OnlyOneClient but after the grants at :358-359 it only exercises myclient (:362, :364) and never tries realmClient, unlike the sibling testManageOnlyOneClient (:180-188) which does assert ForbiddenException on realmClient. Astra's citations (RolePermissions.java:308/:398, ClientPermissionsV2.java:214-220) show head isolates clients correctly, which I do not dispute; they are exactly the code a regression would change without this test noticing. ev/2 runs the test's steps against a client-ignoring canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles: every step passes while realmClient gets OK/OK instead of 403/403. The test cannot fail on the one property its name claims, so it is TP (test_gap).
evidenciaV4.astra: Changed to TP (test_gap). The PR adds this test, but PermissionClientTest.java:343–364 checks only myclient before and after granting permission; it never checks that another client remains forbidden. Thus it does not verify the client isolation its stated scope requires. My earlier verdict incorrectly required a production failure for a test defect.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: testConfigureOnlyOneClient grants CONFIGURE only on myclient, and every post-grant operation targets myclient. The test would still pass if canConfigure ignored the client argument and applied the grant to every client.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reasonUpstreamV4: PR #38639 ("[FGAP:V2] remove configure scope from Client resource type") deleted testConfigureOnlyOneClient together with the configure scope. CLIENTS on main no longer has CONFIGURE, and canConfigure redirects to canManage.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: After granting all-clients MANAGE, testManageAllClients asserts only that the client listing is not empty. It would pass if the endpoint omitted some authorized clients.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reasonUpstreamV4: testManageAllClients on main (ClientResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:330-361) still ends with "can list & view all clients" and assertThat(found, not(empty())). Main now grants VIEW and MANAGE, but the assertion is unchanged.

evidenciaV4.opus: I agree head lists all clients (ev/4 shows 8/8); the defect is the test, not head, and RUBRICA.md counts 'a test that does not verify the behaviour it was written for' as TP. The comment at PermissionClientTest.java:278 says 'can list & view all clients' but :280 asserts only not(empty()). Partial listings are a realistic failure mode here: with all-clients MANAGE, ClientPermissionsV2.java:86-88 makes canView() false, so ClientsResource.java:148 filters every client through per-client canView(c), and the per-resource lookup at ClientPermissionsV2.java:214-221 is exactly where an omission would arise. ev/4 shows a listing of 1 of 8 clients passes the assertion, so the 'all clients' claim is never checked.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: After granting all-clients VIEW, testViewAllClients asserts only not(empty()) on the client listing. It would pass if only myclient were exposed instead of all clients.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reasonUpstreamV4: testViewAllClients on main (ClientResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:496-536) still asserts only not(empty()) on findAll(true) after the all-clients VIEW grant, and the follow-up checks touch only myclient.

evidenciaV4.opus: Astra's trace (ClientPermissionsV2.java:86-87, ClientsResource.java:122/:148-150) shows head returns all clients, and ev/5 agrees (8/8); that is not in dispute. The defect is that the test cannot detect a violation: PermissionClientTest.java:303-305 says 'can list and view all clients' but asserts only not(empty()), and every later check (:308-320) uses only myclient. ev/5 shows a listing reduced to [myclient] passes every assertion of testViewAllClients, so the all-clients VIEW behaviour the test was written for is never verified. PermissionClientTest.java:303–305 accepts a singleton myclient listing despite intending to verify all-clients VIEW, and subsequent checks never establish visibility of another client. add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: Claims that the CLIENTS type and new scopes are added only to the static schema and that init() skips realms that already have the admin-permissions client. Realms with V2 enabled earlier would then miss the Clients resource and the configure/map-roles scopes, which breaks creating and evaluating client permissions.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reasonUpstreamV4: PR #48320 added ensureSchemaUpToDate() to AdminPermissionsSchema.init(), so an existing admin-permissions client no longer early-returns: missing scopes and type resources (Clients included) are created. MigrateTo26_7_0 calls init() for realms that have the client. Earlier, MigrateTo26_6_2 called init(), which still early-returned.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.prTitle: Add comprehensive email validation for blocked users

prOriginal.nota: No upstream PR: the benchmark head commit 5f8a130277 itself is on discourse/discourse main (compare status 'ahead', behind_by=0), pushed directly on 2013-07-29 (committer date) with no associated pull request (commits/{sha}/pulls empty; PR searches by title and BlockedEmail found nothing). Merged code is identical to the benchmark head.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.bug: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.reason: After the rename to ScreenedEmail (86647f0a54, 2013-08-14) should_block? still did an exact ScreenedEmail.where(email: email) lookup. Commit 'Emails are case insensitive' (01a68f8cc7, 2014-07-16) added before_save :downcase_email to ScreenedEmail, before_validation :downcase_email to User, and compares se.email.downcase with email.downcase in should_block?. Today's screened_email.rb still downcases on save and canonical() downcases the input, so casing no longer bypasses a block.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.bug: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.reason: On main today ScreenedEmail.should_block? still calls screened_email.record_match! on a match, and ScreeningModel#record_match! (lib/screening_model.rb) still does self.match_count += 1, sets last_match_at and calls save: a non-atomic read-modify-write run from EmailValidator during validation. The history of screened_email.rb and screening_model.rb after the merge shows no change to this side effect (only refactors, the levenshtein lookup and annotations).
add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.reasonUpstreamV4: On discourse/discourse main today ScreenedEmail.should_block? still calls record_match!, and ScreeningModel#record_match! still does match_count += 1, sets last_match_at and calls save from inside EmailValidator. Since 2025 the only commits to these files are rubocop and annotation changes (#40095, #39977) and a developer-email check in email_validator.rb (#45618), none of which touch this.

evidenciaV4.opus: Both sides now agree on the facts and the class: the read-modify-save race at app/models/blocked_email.rb:12-16 can lose a match_count increment, but the side effect is intended and tested (spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:26-38), blocking stays correct, and nothing at head reads match_count or last_match_at, so it is a real but inconsequential nit. What is left is a disagreement over rules, not over code. DEBATE-EVIDENCE.md tells this round to apply the rules of evidence in EVIDENCE.md step 2. That step defines TP as 'a defect worth a review comment per RUBRICA.md (TP without subclass)' and says FP covers a finding that 'is only a nit'. RUBRICA.md's own nit definition ('real, but not worth a reviewer's comment') is exactly the subclass that EVIDENCE.md excludes from TP, so the agreed classification of a nit maps to FP in this verdict.
evidenciaV4.astra: Keep TP, subclass nit (category: concurrency). The PR introduces an unlocked read-modify-save at app/models/blocked_email.rb:12–16, so concurrent signup validations can overwrite each other’s match_count increment. Updating statistics is intentional and tested; blocking remains correct, and no application code consumes these statistics. The reviewer’s impact assessment is sound, but your supplied taxonomy explicitly classifies real, inconsequential problems as TP/nit; the quoted EVIDENCE.md rule does not override it.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.bug: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.reason: The unanchored Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) stayed (later "@(.+\\.)?(#{domains})" in PR #3463 and 69ad0358c2, 2015) with no end anchor, so gmail.com.evil.com matched. Commit 'SECURITY: email domain whitelist could be bypassed' (2a22b90538, 2018-01-17) appended $ to the regex, with a spec for email.computers.are.evil.com; today's EmailValidator.email_in_restriction_setting? still uses "@(.+\\.)?(#{domains})$". Subdomain matching (evil.example.com for example.com) is intended behaviour upstream since 2015; the suffix bypass is what was fixed.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.bug: Emails rejected by the server are cached in rejectedEmails for the controller's lifetime and never cleared, so an address that later becomes valid keeps failing client-side validation until reload.
add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.reason: The signup logic moved from create_account_controller.js to controllers/signup.js, and kept the 2013 pattern until mid-2025: rejectedEmails.pushObject(result.values.email) on a server email error, and emailValidation failing on rejectedEmails.includes(email). PR #33072 (merged 2025-08-06, ced043be3c) deleted that pushObject block. The PR is mainly about destination_url cookies and does not explain the deletion. On main today, signup.js still declares rejectedEmails and still checks includes(), but nothing adds to the array, so a server rejection can no longer leave a stale client-side block. The separate invite-acceptance controller (invites/show.js, added later) has its own copy of the pattern; that is a different flow and is not counted here.

astra.pergunta: PR #33072 (cookie handling) deleted the rejectedEmails.pushObject block in signup.js. The array and check remain, but nothing populates them. Is this confirmado or descontinuado, and does the same pattern in invites/show.js make it pendente?
astra.resposta: Confirmado. #33072 removed the population of rejectedEmails, which eliminates the reported behaviour in signup. Under the given definition the fix counts even though it is incidental and the PR does not mention the bug. The cache in invites/show.js belongs to another flow and may deserve a separate investigation, but it does not make this case pendente.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.prTitle: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema

prOriginal.nota: Found with gh search prs by title. The PR has a single commit equal to the benchmark head (7355f05e6a); it was merged into main as 679f44692d with the same commit message, so the merged code matches the benchmark head.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: The merged GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returned hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). PR #38559 '[FGAP] remove transitiveness from auth scopes' changed it to hasPermission(null, MANAGE). Today's main (fgap/GroupPermissionsV2.java) checks only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE in canManage().

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #38015 'Fix permissions for view-members and manage-members' rewrote getGroupIdsWithViewPermission to iterate the resources of the Groups-type policies and call hasPermission(gr.getName(), ...) and granted.add(gr.getName()), so it passes and returns group ids (resource names) instead of resource ids. The method was later turned into an UnsupportedOperationException in the V2 evaluator refactor.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: Per-group resources are created without the Groups type, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's findByType never sees specific group grants.
add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #38015 replaced resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) with policyStore.findByResourceType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) flattened to policy.getResources(), so per-group resources attached to Groups permissions are enumerated even though they carry no type. The fix does not add a type to the resources, but the missing per-group grants behaviour is gone.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: The user search filter still requires legacy 'group.resource.<id>' resources, so with V2 group permissions the members of authorized groups are excluded from user searches.
add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #38015 changed JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery to match the resource name to the bare groupId when admin permissions V2 are enabled for the realm, keeping the 'group.resource.'+groupId pattern only for V1. Members of V2-authorized groups are no longer excluded from the user search filter.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission passes getResourceTypeResource's result to policyStore.findByResource without a null check, causing an NPE and 500 on group listing and user search when the Groups type resource is missing.
add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: The evaluator still dereferences the Groups type resource without a null check (61cb0acbc4 on 2025-04-01 dropped the findByResource(null) call, and today FineGrainedAdminPermissionEvaluator.hasPermission calls resourceTypeResource.getScopes() unguarded). But the trigger, an existing admin-permissions client lacking the Groups type resource because AdminPermissionsSchema.init returned early, was fixed by PR #48320 (2026-04-29): init now runs ensureSchemaUpToDate, creating every missing type resource and scope, and MigrateTo26_7_0 runs it for every realm with FGAP. Issue #49732 (2026-06-05) shows the missing Groups resource happened in real upgrades; PR #49893 (2026-06-23) also calls init in MigrateTo26_6_2.

astra.pergunta: Confirmado (via #48320 backfill or #49893 migration fix) or pendente since the evaluator has no null check?
astra.resposta: Confirmado by PR #48320 (2026-04-29): the backfill run by the migration removes the condition that triggered the bug; #49893 complements it on the 26.6.2 migration path but is not the first fix.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: Removing the canViewGlobal short-circuit from the subgroup and group listings makes an admin with an all-groups V2 grant run one full authorization evaluation per group in the listing instead of a single check.
add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #38322 ('Support partial evaluation for the group resource type', issue #38273, motivation 'Apply FGAP permissions when querying groups') moved V2 group filtering into the store query and wrapped the per-group canView filter in GroupResource.getSubGroups, GroupsResource.getGroups and GroupUtils.populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups with `if (!isAdminPermissionsEnabled(realm))`. Today's main still has that guard, so under FGAP V2 the listings no longer run one evaluation per group. astra.pergunta: Bug + benchmark code + #38322 diff + today's code; confirmado (fixed by #38322) or descontinuado (rewrite not aimed at this perf issue)?

prOriginal.nota: Found via the commit history of addGuests.handler.ts (first commit baa9045af7, 'feat: ability to add guests via app.cal.com/bookings (#14740)'). PR headRefOid equals the benchmark head and the merged handler is byte-identical to the benchmark head. The repo calcom/cal.com now redirects to calcom/cal.diy.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reason: PR #17017 changed `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` to `||` in addGuests.handler.ts, so team ADMINs pass the check. The check was later replaced by PermissionCheckService (#24026, fallback OWNER/ADMIN) and is absent today, but the fix came first.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reason: PR #24298 rewrote the filter to compare `extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase()` against the lowercased blacklist; today sanitizeAndFilterGuests still does `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(baseGuestEmail)` with the lowercased input, so mixed case no longer bypasses it.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reason: PR #24298 added a Set-based dedup of input guests by lowercased base email (now deduplicateGuestEmails), so repeated emails in one request are collapsed before createMany.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: Check-then-insert without a transaction or unique constraint lets two concurrent addGuests calls for the same email both pass the existing-attendee check and create duplicate attendees.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reason: Today the handler still reads booking.attendees, filters in memory, then BookingRepository.updateBookingAttendees runs a separate booking.update with attendees.createMany, no transaction or lock. schema.prisma Attendee still has only indexes on email/bookingId, no unique (bookingId,email), so concurrent requests can both insert.

evidenciaV4.opus: Astra's round-4 argument is the same as round 2, and my reply still stands. I don't dispute the mechanics: ev/1 reproduces the duplicate when both calls fire together (read at addGuests.handler.ts:26, insert at :92, no composite unique key at schema.prisma:526). To trigger it, though, an organizer and an attendee have to submit the same previously absent email independently, both landing in the few-round-trip window between :26 and :92 (the isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner checks at :46-48 and findFirstOrThrow at :58). Two people choosing the same address within tens of milliseconds isn't a realistic input, and the result is a visible duplicate row the organizer can remove. EVIDENCE.md requires a realistic triggering input for TP and says FP when in doubt, so I keep FP.
evidenciaV4.astra: Keep TP (concurrency). The new handler reads attendees at line 26, filters against that snapshot at line 74, and inserts at line 92 without atomic uniqueness enforcement; Attendee has no booking/email unique constraint. An organizer and authenticated attendee can submit overlapping requests, and the dialog’s pending state only protects its own instance. The reviewer’s reproduction confirms persistent duplicates; a short race window and recoverable impact do not eliminate this reachable defect.

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: Collective team booking: organizer host1, co-host host2 persisted as an Attendee row (createBooking.ts getAttendeesData pushes evt.team.members into attendees), booker, plus new guest newguest@x.com | observed: OrganizerAddGuests -> host1; AttendeeAddGuests -> booker and host2 (subject name 'Host One'); AttendeeScheduled -> newguest. host2 notified: true | expected: Per the claim, host2 would get no guests-added email; actually host2 is notified, only via the attendee variant with the organizer's name in place of the team name in the subject. | addGuests.handler.ts:92-120 builds evt.attendees from all booking Attendee rows, and createBooking.ts:143-162 (getAttendeesData) stores team members as Attendee rows, so email-manager.ts:539-547 sends them AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. The dead team branch at email-manager.ts:531 only changes which template they get and the name in the subject (attendee-add-guests-email.ts uses team?.name || organizer.name). The claimed effect (team hosts never notified) does not happen; what remains is cosmetic.

The subject uses Alice’s name instead of the team name. | expected: Bob receives the guests-added notification, which already happens; using the team name would improve wording. | Additional hosts are included in evt.team at packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1025, then persisted as attendees by packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/createBooking.ts:153 and :219. The new handler reloads all attendees at packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 and maps them into the event at :108, so packages/emails/email-manager.ts:539 sends Bob the notification despite skipping the team branch. The organizer-name fallback at packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts:24 is real, but the remaining subject-wording discrepancy does not establish a review-worthy defect under the requested threshold.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: Claimed: different errors for unknown vs unauthorized booking ids let any authenticated user enumerate valid booking ids.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reasonUpstreamV4: On main, getBooking still looks the booking up by id alone and throws NOT_FOUND 'booking_not_found', and validateUserPermissions then throws FORBIDDEN, so the two errors still differ.

evidenciaV4.opus: I concede TP, subclass nit (security). My own run shows the oracle: the new handler's unscoped lookup at addGuests.handler.ts:26 returns NOT_FOUND (:44) for a missing id and FORBIDDEN (:54-55) for an existing one the caller cannot access. In RUBRICA.md, nit is a subclass of TP, not of FP, so my argument (real, but nit-level hardening) actually supports TP-nit rather than FP. The impact is still limited, since only existence leaks, through dense autoincrement ids, with no booking content, owner or write access.
evidenciaV4.astra: Keep TP, but classify it as nit (security). The new handler demonstrably distinguishes nonexistent IDs from existing, inaccessible bookings through NOT_FOUND versus FORBIDDEN. Autoincrement IDs make existence predictable without eliminating that disclosure, but the reviewer correctly limits its impact: no booking details or ownership are exposed. This merits hardening, not a substantive security finding.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: updateCalendarAttendees discards calendar-provider failures, so addGuestsHandler reports success and sends emails while the external calendar event never got the new guests.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reasonUpstreamV4: On main, EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees still returns void after awaiting updateAllCalendarEvents, and the handler's updateCalendarEvent ignores the outcome before sending notifications.

evidenciaV4.opus: I keep FP. The facts are not in dispute: EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees (EventManager.ts:596-602, untouched) discards success:false. But that is the codebase's intended best-effort calendar sync, which createNewSeat.ts:147 and attendeeRescheduleSeatedBooking.ts:39/:92 rely on in the same way, so the rubric's 'behaviour that is intended' / untouched-code ruling applies. Astra's new retry point is only partly right. Re-submitting the same email does hit BAD_REQUEST (handler:74-80), but any later addGuests or reschedule rebuilds evt.attendees from the full DB list (handler:108-140) and pushes the complete list to the provider, so the stale state recovers on the next sync. Meanwhile the guest is committed and gets the invite by email (handler:168), so this is a transient provider outage handled the way the rest of the codebase handles it, not a defect this PR introduces.
evidenciaV4.astra: Change to FP. The failure trace is accurate, but the unchanged updateCalendarAttendees helper already provides best-effort synchronization, and existing seat creation and rescheduling callers likewise proceed without checking provider success. The new handler commits the guests and sends invitations consistently with that contract; no changed failure mechanism is demonstrated. A later successful addition rebuilds the complete attendee list, so my earlier retry argument does not establish unrecoverable inconsistency.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: The add-guests action and handler ignore eventType.disableGuests and seatsPerTimeSlot, so guests can be added to events where guests are disabled and to seated events without a seat record.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reasonUpstreamV4: PR #24414 added validateGuestsFieldEnabled, which rejects with BAD_REQUEST when the event type's 'guests' booking field is hidden. That is how disableGuests is expressed (getBookingFields.ts maps disableGuests to guests.hidden), so hosts who disabled guests are now enforced. The seatsPerTimeSlot half is still unchecked on main.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: sendAddGuestsEmails builds attendee emails without showAttendees, so for seated events the email hides other attendees even when seatsShowAttendees is enabled.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reasonUpstreamV4: PR #27520 ('filter attendees in emails when seatsShowAttendees is disabled') changed the AttendeeScheduledEmail constructor (also inherited by AttendeeAddGuestsEmail). When showAttendees is undefined it now falls back to calEvent.seatsShowAttendees, so the add-guests emails show attendees when seatsShowAttendees is true.

add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.bug: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.
add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.reason: Commit 3e0bb6df 'Fix range error when minimizing the string' (PR #38779, closes #38778) changed the suffix loop bounds from end < sanitized.length() && end < value.length() to end < sanitized.length() - start && end < value.length() - start, so prefix and suffix can no longer overlap and substring cannot throw. Today's VerifyMessageProperties keeps that bound.

add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.bug: normalizeValue blanks the entire choice expression for some keys before HTML validation, so markup placed inside a choice branch of those keys bypasses the new verifier.
add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.reason: normalizeValue on main still does value.replaceAll("\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}", "...") for keys starting with linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit and for error-invalid-multivalued-size, before santizeAnchors and the HTML policy run. Markup inside those choice branches is still never checked.
add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.reasonUpstreamV4: normalizeValue still blanks {n,choice,...} on main, but markup in a choice branch only renders if quoted with lone single quotes (unquoted '<' makes ChoiceFormat throw 'Choice Pattern incorrect', ev/3/probe), and PR #37931 ('Validate single quotes in themes', 2025-03-17) added verifyMessageFormatQuotes, enabled for themes/ in themes/pom.xml, which rejects lone single quotes; the bypassing translation now fails the build (ev/3/probe/output.txt: flagged=true). add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.bug: The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

The verifier also now rejects single-brace placeholders for frontend bundles (verifyNotMessageFormatPlaceholders).

add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.bug: If the English counterpart of a messages_*.properties file does not exist, verifySafeHtml throws an unchecked RuntimeException that escapes the mojo, crashing the build instead of reporting a validation message.

add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.reasonUpstreamV4: On main the English path is now built by resolveEnglishReferenceFile (PF6 commit 66cf7c96, 2026-11-12) and a missing file still throws new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile); verify() catches only IOException and ThemeVerifierMojo does not catch it.

However, ThemeVerifierMojo.java:55 also fails the build for ordinary validation errors, so the stated alternative does not establish a different functional outcome. All 162 inspected production message bundles have their derived English counterpart, leaving an exception-reporting improvement rather than a demonstrated build regression.

add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.bug: The theme verifier's HTML and anchor regexes are case-sensitive, so uppercase tags in translations are flagged as illegal HTML by the build.
add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.reason: On keycloak/keycloak main today, misc/theme-verifier/.../VerifyMessageProperties.java still declares ANCHOR_PATTERN = Pattern.compile("</?a[^>]*>") (and HTML_TAGS "<[a-z]+[^>]*>") with no CASE_INSENSITIVE flag, and santizeAnchors still only strips anchors matched by it. POLICY_SOME_HTML still allows only br/p/strong/b/formattedLink (no anchors), so an uppercase <A ...> identical in English and translation survives santizeAnchors, gets stripped by the sanitizer and reported as 'Illegal HTML'. The 10 later commits to the file (2025-02-23 to 2026-01-20) add other validations (blanks, quotes, placeholders, curly braces, discouraged words) and do not touch the anchor/HTML patterns.
add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.reasonUpstreamV4: On main HTML_TAGS is still Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>") and ANCHOR_PATTERN still Pattern.compile("</?a[^>]*>"), both case-sensitive; no later commit touches them.

evidenciaV4.opus: Astra's trace is right about the mechanism (VerifyMessageProperties.java:139/:145 are case-sensitive, so <A href> gets stripped by POLICY_NO_HTML at :92 and reported at :99), but the outcome is a loud, build-time rejection, not a silent acceptance. git grep over every messages_*.properties at the head finds no uppercase HTML tags, so no existing or realistic input hits this. A build-time safety check that is stricter than needed fails closed, and the maintainer fixes it by lowercasing the tag. No runtime or user effect and no unsafe HTML gets through, so this is a robustness nit and stays FP.
evidenciaV4.astra: Changing my verdict to FP. The regexes are case-sensitive, but the actual message bundles contain no uppercase HTML tags; the uppercase placeholders and choice expressions are explicitly normalized. My earlier example established hypothetical rejection without demonstrating an affected real caller input, as required here. A build-time rejection can be a defect, but the evidence does not establish one for this PR.

add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.bug: The anchor regex </?a[^>]*> in the theme verifier treats any tag starting with 'a' (<abbr>, <area>, ...) as an anchor tag, which can produce misleading anchor errors or strip such tags before HTML sanitizing.
add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.reason: On keycloak/keycloak main today, VerifyMessageProperties.java still declares ANCHOR_PATTERN = Pattern.compile("</?a[^>]*>") and santizeAnchors still strips matched tags (so <abbr>, <area>, etc. are treated as anchors) before the OWASP policy runs in verifySafeHtml. The 10 commits on this file since the merge (RTL autodetect, blanks, single quotes, placeholders, curly braces, range fix, import order, referrer-policy text, login escaping, whitelist wording) never touch the anchor regex or santizeAnchors; the only policy change added 'formattedLink' to the allowed elements.
add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.reasonUpstreamV4: On main ANCHOR_PATTERN is still "</?a[^>]*>" and santizeAnchors still removes matching tags present in the English value before the OWASP policy runs.

evidenciaV4.opus: Conceding: Astra's bypass trace holds, and I reproduced it (ev/C1/Main.java is a verbatim copy of :139-162; output in ev/C1/out.txt). When messages_en.properties is verified against itself (:74-75, same flow VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected relies on), ANCHOR_PATTERN at :145 matches <audio ...>, </audio>, <abbr>, and <area href="javascript:...">. santizeAnchors removes all of them at :155 without reporting anything, so no tags reach the policy at :92 and no 'Illegal HTML' error is raised. <script> in the same position is still caught. So the verifier silently accepts any disallowed tag starting with 'a' in English sources, which it is explicitly meant to reject, and translations copying that tag then pass the identical-anchor check too. I had argued FP because no bundle contains such a tag today, but the defect defeats the check's own purpose for a whole class of tags.

The pattern at :145 matches both audio tags, and the identical-source comparison at :154 removes them at :155 before the policy runs at :92. Consequently, the whitelist at :60 never sees the prohibited element and :99 finds no difference. VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java:37 explicitly tests rejection of disallowed HTML in an English bundle, confirming that English-source validation is part of this verifier's behavior.

anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.bug: Device slots are keyed by the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header with no validation or rate limiting, so an anonymous caller can fill the limit with fake IDs and deny anonymous access to every new legitimate device.

anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.reasonUpstreamV4: impl.go TagDevice on main still takes X-Grafana-Device-Id verbatim and tagDeviceUI admits new IDs until ErrDeviceLimitReached; #94218 (cache) and #94700 (validator) add no ID validation or per-client rate limit.

evidenciaV4.opus: I re-checked astra's trace at the head and it is accurate: impl.go:119/136 takes the header verbatim, database.go:110-116 admits fake-A/fake-B, and client.go:45 fails real-C with ErrDeviceLimitReached. That outcome is still the contract of the feature, not a defect in the code: anonymous visitors have no verifiable identity, so a cap on 'anonymous devices' can only count client-declared IDs, and any such cap can be filled by whoever reaches it first, real or fake. The PR does not claim the limit is an abuse-resistant admission control, and the alternatives (IP binding, fingerprinting) are just as client-controlled or break NAT'd users. Astra itself notes the cache inserted before admission (impl.go:87) lets the next request through, so the 'denial' is one failed first request under an operator-chosen cap. That is a threat-model limit of an unauthenticated usage cap, not a realistic-input defect, so under 'when in doubt, FP' I keep FP.
evidenciaV4.astra: Changed to FP (no subclass). The code accepts distinct client-supplied IDs until capacity is exhausted, but that demonstrates the configured device-count policy rather than a separate violation of it. Neither validation nor a reliable one-client/one-device identity contract is established here. The cache also allows subsequent requests from rejected IDs, so the claimed blanket denial overstates the actual behavior.

async-import-of-the-appstore-packages-ca.bug: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
async-import-of-the-appstore-packages-ca.reason: PR #10157 'fix: replace all async foreach callbacks' replaced the forEach(async ...) loops in vital/lib/reschedule.ts, wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and the trpc requestReschedule handler (where bookings.tsx's reschedule moved) with map(async ...) plus await Promise.all / Promise.allSettled, so getCalendar failures are awaited and caught. Today both reschedule.ts files still use const promises = bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...) followed by await Promise.all(promises) inside try/catch.

async-import-of-the-appstore-packages-ca.bug: Each import(...) in the appStore object literal runs when app-store/index.ts is imported, so all integrations still load at startup instead of lazily, while every entry becomes a promise.

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: SQLite, cleanupjob_batchsize=32767 (the PR's own test value, cleanup_test.go:101), a full batch of 32767 ids. | observed: ev/2 (head loop xorm_store.go:609-612 verbatim): batch 32767 takes 1.30 s and allocates 7424.6 MB to build a 226604-byte list; batch 10000: 66 ms / 425 MB; strings.Builder gives identical output in 0.6 ms / 1.4 MB. | expected: Linear-time construction of the IN list (strings.Builder or strings.Join). | xorm_store.go:608 takes the literal-ID path exactly when SQLite and batch size > 999, the case this PR adds for large batches, and :611 re-copies the whole accumulated string per id, so cost grows quadratically (10x ids -> ~20x time, ~1000x allocation from 1000 to 32767). Gigabytes of allocation and over a second of CPU per batch on the path the PR introduces is a meaningful performance defect, not a micro-optimisation.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: SQLite, cleanupjob_batchsize=32767, API MaxCount=1, and API annotations with IDs 1 through 32768. | observed: Cleanup formats IDs 32767 through 1 into a 218261-byte list. The intermediate formatted strings contain 3707416662 bytes cumulatively, before executing the DELETE. | expected: Construct the same list with approximately linear copying and allocation. | API-created annotations reach storage through pkg/api/annotations.go:244 and pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:70; cleanup.go:43 then reaches xorm_store.go:549, selecting these 32767 victims. xorm_store.go:608 selects literal formatting, and :611 copies the entire accumulated prefix on every iteration. Summing those exact output lengths establishes gigabytes of cumulative string allocation for one modest batch, a meaningful performance regression rather than a micro-optimisation.

database-performance-optimizations-grafa.bug: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.
database-performance-optimizations-grafa.reason: The same PR #80670 (merged 2024-01-16) reverted the ticker in pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go from time.Minute * 1 back to time.Minute * 10; main today still has time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10).

database-performance-optimizations-grafa.reason: On main today cleanup_test.go still seeds fresh annotations per subtest (createTestAnnotations inside t.Run) and wipes both tables in t.Cleanup, and the 'running the max count delete again should not remove any annotations' case still calls cleaner.Run once on 9 annotations with MaxCount=3. Later edits to the test (#102622, #106676, #120207, etc.) did not restore a second run.
database-performance-optimizations-grafa.reasonUpstreamV4: cleanup_test.go on main still seeds fresh annotations per subtest, wipes tables in t.Cleanup, and the 'running the max count delete again' case runs cleaner.Run once on 9 annotations with MaxCount=3.

evidenciaV4.opus: [desk] input: Subtest 'running the max count delete again should not remove any annotations': 9 seeded annotations (3 per type), MaxCount=3, batch size 1. | observed: cleanup_test.go:116-118 seeds 9 rows; :132 Run reaches xorm_store.go:547-549 with OFFSET 3 for each type, fetchIDs returns nothing, deleteByIDs (:598-599) returns 0; the test asserts 0 affected and 3 per type remain. | expected: A database already at the MaxCount limit must be left unchanged, which is what a second run would see and what the test asserts. | In the base, the case relied on the previous subtest leaving 3 per type; at head it seeds that same at-limit state directly (cleanup_test.go:83-96, :116-128). Cleanup is a function of table state only, so running on a fresh at-limit table checks the same no-op behaviour as running a second time; nothing about the behaviour is left unverified, only the name's wording differs. Not a defect.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: Run the named subtest with its nine seeded annotations, three of each annotation type, and MaxCount=3 for every type. | observed: Each selection returns no IDs; cleanup reports zero deletions and preserves all nine annotations and eighteen tags. | expected: An already-at-limit database remains unchanged, which the test verifies. | pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:84 seeds nine rows, and :251 and :256 distribute them equally across the three types. Cleanup carries no previous-run state relevant to selection, so this exercises the same no-op boundary as running it again after successful cleanup; the stale name alone is not a reportable defect.

database-performance-optimizations-grafa.bug: The annotation cleanup loop stops on a batch whose IDs were already deleted by a concurrent cleaner, leaving the remaining work to the next cycle; checking the fetched count instead would avoid that.
database-performance-optimizations-grafa.reason: On grafana/grafana main today (last file commit e9243f551a, 2026-09-30), CleanAnnotations/CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags still run fetchIDs then return deleteByIDs, which returns res.RowsAffected(), and untilDoneOrCancelled still stops when affected == 0. None of the 28 commits touching xorm_store.go since the merge changed this loop or the stop condition, so a batch whose fetched IDs were all deleted concurrently still ends cleanup while eligible rows remain.
database-performance-optimizations-grafa.reasonUpstreamV4: deleteByIDs, untilDoneOrCancelled and the CleanAnnotations fetchIDs/deleteByIDs batches are unchanged on grafana/grafana main today (file read 2026-11-13; 30 commits to xorm_store.go since 2024-01-12, latest 80b97080eb on 2026-11-04, none touching them).

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: Two cleaners run MaxCount cleanup concurrently on 20 rows, MaxCount=3, batch 2; both fetch the same batch and the other cleaner deletes it first. | observed: ev/4 (untilDoneOrCancelled verbatim from xorm_store.go:643-661): cleaner B gets affected=0 and stops with 18 rows left, but cleaner A, whose delete affected those rows, keeps looping and ends with 3 rows left (= MaxCount). | expected: All excess rows removed in the cycle, which happens. | untilDoneOrCancelled stops on affected==0 (xorm_store.go:656-657), but a batch can only return 0 because some other deleter removed exactly those rows; when that deleter is another cleaner it got affected>0 and continues to completion, so the work is still done. The only other deleter is a user deleting exactly all fetched ids in a millisecond window, and even then the rest is cleaned next cycle, which the PR's comment (xorm_store.go:523-525) explicitly accepts. No realistic wrong outcome.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: Two instances clean expired annotation IDs 1, 2, and 3 with batch size 1. Both fetch ID 3; cleaner B deletes it before cleaner A executes its DELETE. | observed: A receives zero affected rows and stops. B receives one affected row and continues deleting IDs 2 and 1. | expected: The eligible annotations are cleaned without requiring both overlapping workers to independently exhaust the table. | pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:529 selects ID 3, :626 obtains the affected count, and :656 stops only the worker whose DELETE made no progress. The successful worker continues at :650, so the claimed interleaving alone does not leave unfinished cleanup. If that worker is subsequently cancelled, deferred work is consistent with the cancellation path at :647, the explicit allowance for deferred cleanup at :525, and recurring execution in pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77.

database-performance-optimizations-grafa.reason: On main today CleanAnnotations' MaxCount branch still runs fetchIDs with ORDER BY id DESC LimitOffset(batch, MaxCount) and then deleteByIDs, a separate DELETE ... WHERE id IN (...) in its own session with no re-check or transaction. Later commits to xorm_store.go only removed the debug logs (#80670) and touched unrelated query/tag/migration code.
database-performance-optimizations-grafa.reasonUpstreamV4: deleteByIDs, untilDoneOrCancelled and the CleanAnnotations fetchIDs/deleteByIDs batches are unchanged on grafana/grafana main today (file read 2026-11-13; 30 commits to xorm_store.go since 2024-01-12, latest 80b97080eb on 2026-11-04, none touching them).

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: 10 annotations of one type, MaxCount=3; a user deletes the newest annotation (id 10) between fetchIDs and deleteByIDs. | observed: ev/5: racy interleaving leaves [9 8]; running cleanup first and then the user deletion serially also leaves [9 8]; 'racy result equals a valid serial order: true'. | expected: Any outcome equivalent to a serial order of cleanup and the user's delete, which is what happens. | xorm_store.go:547-556 picks victims from a snapshot at fetch time and deletes only those ids; the result is exactly what an atomic cleanup at fetch time followed by the user's delete would produce, so no annotation is lost beyond what a legal ordering would delete. Later batches re-rank with OFFSET MaxCount on current state, so retention is not undercut further. The 'over-delete' is a valid linearization, not data loss.
