ID 1 was outside the newest three when cleanup selected its victims. | expected: This is a valid result of cleanup removing excess ID 1 followed by the overlapping explicit deletion of ID 4; MaxCount does not guarantee a minimum population. | pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:549 selects ID 1, while pkg/api/annotations.go:522 can independently invoke the deletion implemented at xorm_store.go:419. Cleanup subsequently deletes its selected victim at :622, producing the same final state as executing cleanup before the overlapping user deletion. conf/defaults.ini:1352 defines a maximum count, and this trace establishes neither deletion of a retained snapshot member nor a requirement to replace explicitly deleted retained annotations.

prOriginal.nota: Found via gh pr list by author leonorfmartins ("Dual writer: mode 3", branch dualwriter_mode3). Its headRefOid is e369f24665ec, the benchmark head; squash-merged as 67b74e1e8a. The mode3 file was deleted on 2025-03-01 (#101393) and folded into pkg/storage/legacysql/dualwrite/dualwriter.go.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.bug: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.reason: In #93852 (Dual Writer simplification) the legacy DeleteCollection path moved to deleteCollectionFromLegacyStorage, which records the legacy call via d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...); the swapped recordStorageDuration call on the legacy result is gone. Intermediate commits (#91041, #91113, #92654) only changed the label argument and kept the wrong helper.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.bug: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.reason: The success path of Delete kept passing `name` as the kind/resource label through #91041, #91113, #92654 and #93852 (which even widened it to recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, name, ...)). #98147 rewrote Delete and records storage duration with d.resource, removing the per-object label.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.bug: On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.
dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.reason: In #93852 Create and Update record the Storage call with d.recordStorageDuration(errObjectSt != nil / err != nil, ...) right after the d.Storage call; the recordLegacyDuration call on the storage failure branch was removed in both methods.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.bug: Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.
dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.reason: #93852 moved the legacy writes into helper goroutines whose context is context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 10s, ...), with an explicit comment that it ignores cancellation from the parent context; request completion no longer cancels the legacy write. #98147 later made the writes synchronous.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.bug: Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.
dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.reason: The raw objInfo passed to Legacy.Update survived until #98147, which rewrote mode 3 Update to write legacy first (as primary) and unified second, both from objInfo. The step where legacy should persist the unified result but recomputes it no longer exists; today's pkg/storage/legacysql/dualwrite/dualwriter.go keeps the legacy-first order with unified recomputing via wrappedUpdateInfo. Not a change targeting this bug, so descontinuado.

astra.pergunta: Given base (updateWrapper with storage result), head (raw objInfo to legacy in goroutine), #98147 (legacy first, then unified, both with objInfo) and today's dualWriter.Update: confirmado, pendente or descontinuado?
astra.resposta: descontinuado: #98147 writes legacy first, removing the stage where legacy should persist the unified result; stores can still diverge, but now the unified store recomputes, not the original behaviour; a rewrite, not a targeted fix.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.bug: The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.
dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.reason: #98147 made the legacy writes synchronous, so the tests no longer race with a goroutine, and #100389 (use dedicated mocks per storage type) replaced the shared *mock.Mock with one mock per backend, whose description cites exactly the shared-mock problem. Today's dualwriter_mode3_test.go uses separate fakeStorage instances, and legacy-failure cases expect an error that only the legacy fake can produce.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.bug: Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.
dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.reason: #98147 (Block on legacy writes in mode3) removed the per-request goroutines for Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection; legacy and unified writes now run synchronously in the request, so writes to the same resource keep request order.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.bug: DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.
dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.reason: #98147 rewrote Delete to delete from legacy first, tolerating apierrors.IsNotFound from legacy, and only then from unified storage. An object present only in legacy is now deleted there before the unified NotFound is returned, so the early return that skipped the legacy delete is gone.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.bug: Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.
dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.reason: Up to 66e0121dd5 (2024-08-29) the mode-3 goroutines for Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection still only called recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...) with no log. PR #93852 'Dual Writer simplification' (2024-10-23) moved them into createOnLegacyStorage/deleteFromLegacyStorage/updateOnLegacyStorage/deleteCollectionFromLegacyStorage, each with log.Error(err, "unable to ... in legacy storage"), restoring legacy error logging. Later #98147 made legacy writes blocking and #101393 (2025-03-01) folded the file into legacysql/dualwrite, after the fix.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.bug: TestMode3_Get and TestMode3_List share one mock.Mock between the legacy and storage mocks with identical method names, so they would still pass if Mode 3 read from LegacyStorage instead of Storage.
dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.reasonUpstreamV4: PR #100389 'fix(unified-storage): use dedicated mocks per storage type' replaced the shared `m := &mock.Mock{}` in TestMode3_Get/TestMode3_List (and the other mode tests) with `legacyStoreMock{&mock.Mock{}, l}` / `storageMock{&mock.Mock{}, s}`, setting expectations on ls.Mock and us.Mock separately, so reads are now pinned to Storage.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.bug: The new Mode 3 playlist integration subtests set DualWriterDesiredModes to Mode3, but SetDualWritingMode defaults a fresh key to Mode1 and only handles Mode1<->Mode2 transitions, so the subtests silently run in Mode1 and Mode3 cannot be enabled through configuration.
dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.reasonUpstreamV4: PR #95968 ('Allow downgrade from any mode to mode 1 or 2. Allow setting all dual writer combinations') replaced the 1<->2-only transitions and the '#TODO add support for other combinations' in SetDualWritingMode with a switch that includes `desiredMode >= Mode3 && currentMode < Mode3` (run the data syncer, then set and return desiredMode), so a fresh key defaulted to Mode1 now moves to Mode3 when Mode3 is desired. Before that, #89809 (2024-08-27) had only added 2->3, which still left fresh instances in Mode1.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.prTitle: Enhance embed URL handling and validation system

prOriginal.nota: Benchmark head 4f8aed2 is itself on upstream main: direct commit by Robin Ward, 2013-12-31 ('FEATURE: Embeddable Discourse comments, now with simple-rss instead of feedzirra'), no PR associated (gh commits/<sha>/pulls empty). Base 62db063 is the revert of the earlier attempt; diff identical to the benchmark.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: embed.js moved to public/javascripts/embed.js (2013-12-31) and was rewritten many times, but postMessageReceived on main still accepts any message whose origin is a substring of the Discourse URL: `if (!normalizeUrl(DE.discourseUrl).includes(normalizeUrl(e.origin))) return;` (indexOf became includes in #17541). The substring origin check that lets a prefix origin set the iframe height is unchanged.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: public/javascripts/embed.js on main (2d0e900, 2026-11-13) still returns early only when `!normalizeUrl(DE.discourseUrl).includes(normalizeUrl(e.origin))`, a substring test; the 2026 changes to the file (#36613, #39297, #39321) touched the resize handling, not the origin check.

evidenciaV4.opus: I concede. ev/1 shows that embed.js:17, a file this PR adds, accepts any origin that is a string prefix of discourseUrl, so an attacker who registers https://forum.example.co gets past the check for https://forum.example.com. With height=1 on the non-scrolling iframe, the attacker can hide the comments. The golden's evil-<host> example is wrong, but the issue it describes, an indexOf origin check that can be bypassed, is real and reachable with a domain anyone can register. Its only sink is the resize, but RUBRICA counts a security problem as TP without subclass, and a reviewer would flag this check.
evidenciaV4.astra: Keep TP (security; no subclass). embed.js:17 accepts https://forum.example.co for discourseUrl=https://forum.example.com/, and height=1 hides the non-scrolling comments iframe. Opening the publisher in a separate window gives the attacker a messaging reference, not permission to obscure that window’s contents; this handler supplies that unauthorized capability. The illustrative evil-domain example is incorrect, but the origin-validation bypass exists.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: The SiteSetting comparisons were replaced by EmbeddableHost.record_for_url on 2015-08-18 (d1c69189, `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`), which fixed a mixed-case admin host but still did not downcase the incoming URI host. PR #17840 made UrlHelper.escape_uri/normalized_encode (used by record_for_url and url_allowed?) downcase the host via normalize_with_ruby_uri, so both referer and embed_url checks are case-insensitive on main today.

astra.pergunta: #04: confirmado at 2015-08-18 (EmbeddableHost where lower(host)=?, incoming host not downcased) or 2022-08-09 (PR #17840 normalize_with_ruby_uri downcases incoming host)?
astra.resposta: Confirmado at PR #17840, 2022-08-09: it lowercases the incoming host; after 2015 an uppercase URL host still failed.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: Two days after the original commit, ed2e53bb ('FIX: Support feeds with description as well as content') replaced `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with `content = i.content || i.description; if content ... end`, removing the nil.scrub crash. PollFeed was later moved to the rss-polling plugin (#8233).

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: Posts imported from RSS or remote pages use cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw HTML without sanitization, and the embed view outputs it with raw post.cooked, allowing stored XSS from imported content.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: Post#cook on main still does `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and TopicEmbed.import still defaults cook_method to raw_html (unless embed_support_markdown). RSS import moved to plugins/discourse-rss-polling (#8233), whose FeedItem#cook_method returns nil for HTML items, so feed HTML is still stored as cooked without sanitization; the only PrettyText.sanitize added (#42808, 2026-08-25) is on the expansion path, not the stored post.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: Post#cook on main still does `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb:378) and TopicEmbed.import still defaults to raw_html; #42808 (2026-08-25) added PrettyText.sanitize only on the expansion path, and its description is about content fidelity, not security.

evidenciaV4.opus: Astra's sink correction is right: plain.html.erb:14 renders the cooked HTML and FilterBestPosts excludes the first post. That does not change the source, though. The HTML comes only from SiteSetting.feed_polling_url (poll_feed.rb:29) or from pages whose host equals SiteSetting.embeddable_host (topic_retriever.rb:15), which is the admin's own blog or feed. Keeping that raw HTML is the documented design ('we support raw HTML', post.rb:133). Astra's input needs an attacker who already writes content to the admin's trusted feed, and no untrusted caller can supply it, so I keep FP.
evidenciaV4.astra: Change to FP under the required reachability standard. The RSS path preserves executable HTML, but the supplied example assumes attacker-controlled content in the administrator-configured feed without establishing that capability. Remote imports apply Readability's tag/attribute whitelist, and FilterBestPosts excludes the imported first post from the claimed embed sink. The alternative plain-topic sink confirms unsafe rendering if malicious HTML arrives, but does not establish the missing untrusted producer.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: The nil-contents part was fixed on 2015-05-06 (edae9d7a, `contents ||= ''`, today `contents.to_s`). The unescaped URL in the 'imported from' link survived the move into imported_from_html until PR #42314 ('SECURITY: Escape embed URL for HTML attribute context in footer'), which applies ERB::Util.html_escape after URL normalization; that matches the injection described.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: TopicEmbed.import checks for an existing embed and then creates the post and TopicEmbed without handling the unique-index conflict, so two concurrent imports of the same URL make one job fail with RecordNotUnique.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: TopicEmbed.import on main still does an unlocked topic_embed_by_url lookup and then creates the post/embed inside Topic.transaction with no mutex and no rescue of the unique violation; fb8ba5e1 (2015-06-15) only added validates_uniqueness_of (application-level, not race-safe). The synchronous PollFeed inside TopicRetriever was removed with #8233, but the scheduled RSS plugin import and RetrieveTopic/import_remote can still race on the same URL.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: TopicEmbed.import on main still does an unlocked topic_embed_by_url lookup and then PostCreator inside Topic.transaction with no rescue of the unique violation (app/models/topic_embed.rb:73-110); `validates :embed_url, uniqueness: true` is application-level and not race-safe.

evidenciaV4.opus: Astra's new case is an older article that is not in the feed, where the retrieval-triggered poll loses the race and skips fetch_http. New evidence shows this recovers on its own. app/views/embed/loading.html.erb reloads the embed every 30 seconds. Each reload calls EmbedController#best, which enqueues RetrieveTopic again (embed_controller.rb:15), and the throttle key expires after 60 seconds (topic_retriever.rb:28). So within about a minute a new retrieval runs, sees no race, and imports the article. Meanwhile Topic.transaction (topic_embed.rb:21) has already rolled back the loser's duplicate. The result is a logged job exception and up to about a minute more of the existing loading page, with no wrong data and no lasting user-visible failure, so I keep FP.
evidenciaV4.astra: Keep TP (concurrency; no subclass). TopicEmbed.import performs an unprotected lookup followed by create!, so overlapping scheduled and retrieval-triggered polls can raise RecordNotUnique. The requested URL can be an older article absent from the feed: its retrieval polls the feed first, races on a different article, and aborts before fetch_http. The winning poll therefore does not necessarily retrieve the requested article, and transaction rollback does not eliminate the failed job or delayed retrieval.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: 5fb962a6 ('in the case that an imported post was deleted, don't error out of the PollFeed job') changed the update guard to `if post && content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, followed the same day by a post.topic check. Main today returns early with `return post unless post&.topic`.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: Nil contents was handled on 2015-05-06 (edae9d7a). find_remote began rescuing OpenURI::HTTPError on 2017-05-25 (39e19481, then Net::OpenTimeout on 2017-08-10), but import_remote then dereferenced the nil response; PR #5200 added `return if response.nil?` in import_remote, so a dead URL no longer raises. Main keeps both guards.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: PR #14975 ('FIX: Convert URLs embedded topics to absolute form') replaced the start_with?('/') + sub(/^\/+/) rewrite in absolutize_urls with `URI.join(prefix, href)`, which keeps protocol-relative URLs on their own host and resolves path-relative ones (spec changed to images/wat.jpg). Main is unchanged since.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The embed view formats post dates with a hard-coded strftime pattern, so users in non-English locales see English month names and a fixed order while the rest of the view is translated.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: best.html.erb was replaced by EmbedHelper#embed_post_date; PR #28014 (2024-07-22) switched to `dt.strftime I18n.t("datetime_formats.formats.short_no_year")`, which localizes the order, but Ruby strftime %B is not locale-aware and the locale formats use %B (e.g. de '%-d. %B'), so month names still come out in English on main.

astra.pergunta: #24: PR #28014 (2024-07-22) switched to strftime with I18n format strings; %B/%b still English in Ruby strftime. Confirmado or pendente?
astra.resposta: Pendente: #28014 localizes the format order only; month names still come out in English.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: best.html.erb became EmbedHelper#embed_post_date; #28014 (2024-07-22) switched to strftime with I18n datetime formats, fixing the order, but Ruby strftime month names (%b/%B) stay English on main (app/helpers/embed_helper.rb:16-18), so the English month names remain.

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: post created 2013-12-31 viewed by a user whose I18n.locale is de (set in ApplicationController) | observed: ev/4 (LANG=de_DE.UTF-8): '31 Dec 2013' | expected: localized date, e.g. '31. Dez. 2013' (de) / '31 dez 2013' (pt_BR) | best.html.erb:14 formats the date with the literal strftime("%e %b %Y"), which ignores locale, while the same view's labels are translated with I18n.t (lines 3, 5, 25). Every non-English forum shows English month names in the embedded comments, which is a user-visible i18n defect. Upstream later moved the format into I18n (#28014), which confirms it is worth fixing. Low severity.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: A forum configured with default_locale='pt_BR' serves an authorized embed containing a reply created on 2013-02-10. | observed: The reply date renders as '10 Feb 2013', ignoring the configured locale. | expected: Render the date using the Portuguese locale, for example '10/02/2013' using its configured short format. | app/controllers/application_controller.rb:98-99 selects the site's locale, and app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 loads the replies displayed by the embed. app/views/embed/best.html.erb:14 bypasses localization with strftime('%e %b %Y'), producing the English month abbreviation. config/locales/server.pt_BR.yml:12-14 already provides a locale-specific short date format; ignoring the selected language is a user-visible localization defect.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The Disqus importer now creates topics through TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping the thread's created_at and the category option and requiring a live HTTP fetch per thread, so imported topics get wrong dates/categories and a dead link aborts the import.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: disqus.thor moved to script/import_scripts/disqus.rb (efff3351, 2015-07-01) still calling import_remote with the title only. 72d7c055 (2016-08-17) added a hard-coded IMPORT_CATEGORY and a rescue of OpenURI::HTTPError, but on main the thread's created_at is still never applied to the topic or first post, so imported topics still get the import date.

astra.pergunta: #29: 72d7c05 (2016-08-17) added a hard-coded import category and rescue OpenURI::HTTPError around import_remote, but the thread created_at is still never applied. Pendente or confirmado?
astra.resposta: Pendente: partial fix for category and HTTP failures, but the historical topic/first-post date is still dropped.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: lib/tasks/disqus.thor became script/import_scripts/disqus.rb; on main line 67 still calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(t[:link], title: title, user: topic_user)` with no created_at, and only the replies get Date.parse(p[:created_at]) (line 83). 72d7c055 (2016) added a hard-coded category and HTTP error rescue, but the thread date is still dropped.

evidenciaV4.opus: [desk] input: any Disqus export thread with created_at '2011-05-02T...' and its posts | observed: disqus.thor:148 calls TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]); import_remote (topic_embed.rb:44-52) and import (topic_embed.rb:22) pass no created_at or category to PostCreator, so the topic gets import time, while replies keep their historical created_at | expected: topic/first post dated at the thread's created_at and placed in --category, as the removed PostCreator call did (created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id) | The diff removes the --category option and the PostCreator call that kept the thread date, replacing them with import_remote, which has no way to receive either. Every imported thread is therefore dated at import time, after its own replies, and lands uncategorized. The new open(url).read (topic_embed.rb:48) also has no rescue, so one dead link aborts the whole import. This is data-fidelity loss on every run of the importer.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: Import a Disqus export containing a thread dated 2010-02-10, a reply dated 2010-02-11, and a live article URL, on 2013-12-24. | observed: The topic and initial post receive the import date, while the reply retains its historical date and therefore predates its topic. | expected: Preserve the thread's 2010-02-10 creation date on the topic and initial post. | lib/tasks/disqus.thor:60 parses the thread timestamp, but the changed call at :148 passes only its title to import_remote. app/models/topic_embed.rb:52 forwards no timestamp, and its PostCreator call at :22 consequently leaves the timestamp overrides in lib/topic_creator.rb:54 and lib/post_creator.rb:218 unused. Replies still receive their original dates at lib/tasks/disqus.thor:164, proving a chronological regression from the base's explicit created_at argument. The separate claim that title stripping disappeared is incorrect: it remains at lib/tasks/disqus.thor:89.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: 67e20416 ('Prevent topic_retriever from retrieving more than once a minute') changed the throttle key from per-URL `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` to the global `retrieved_topic`, so different unknown articles can no longer each trigger a full synchronous feed poll. The synchronous PollFeed call was later removed entirely with #8233 (2019-11-12).

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The 'is 404 without an embed_url' spec never sets an embeddable host, so the request is rejected by ensure_embeddable before the embed_url check runs, and the test would pass even without that check.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: spec/requests/embed_controller_spec.rb on main still has 'is 404 without an embed_url' doing `get "/embed/comments"` with no embeddable host and asserting only the generic embed.error body. The controller now rejects via `EmbeddableHost.url_allowed?(embed_url)`, which fails for a missing host and a missing URL alike, so the example still cannot detect a missing embed_url check.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: spec/requests/embed_controller_spec.rb on main (lines 203-207) still runs `get "/embed/comments"` with no embeddable host and only matches the generic embed.error body, so the example still cannot tell a missing embed_url from a missing host.

evidenciaV4.opus: [desk] input: the spec 'is 404 without an embed_url' (embed_controller_spec.rb:8-11), with embeddable_host at its default (not stubbed) | observed: before_filter ensure_embeddable (embed_controller.rb:4) raises InvalidAccess at line 25 because embeddable_host is blank, before best runs params.require(:embed_url) at line 9; the spec asserts only should_not be_success (line 10) | expected: with a valid host and referer stubbed, the request fails because embed_url is missing, so deleting params.require makes the spec fail | The example never gets past ensure_embeddable, so it stays green if the embed_url requirement at embed_controller.rb:9 is removed. It also does not check for the 404 its name claims. The test does not verify the behaviour it was written for, which RUBRICA lists as a TP.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: Run the added 'is 404 without an embed_url' example: get :best with no parameters and the default empty embeddable_host. | observed: The request is rejected by the host guard before best executes; removing the embed_url requirement would not change this test's outcome. | expected: Establish a valid host and matching referer so the example exercises missing-parameter handling and detects its removal. | spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8-10 supplies neither host configuration nor a referer, and config/site_settings.yml:354 defaults the allowed host to an empty string. The before_filter at app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:4 therefore raises at :25 before reaching params.require at :9. app/controllers/application_controller.rb:86-87 handles that access error, while the test asserts only generic non-success, leaving its intended validation untested.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: On 2014-04-24 (#2428) the embed_by_username guard and its spec were removed, while 'requires feed_polling_url' kept feed_polling_enabled false and stayed gappy. spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb and Jobs::PollFeed were deleted from core by #8233 (RSS polling moved to a plugin) without a change targeting the gap.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: The same day, cab6a3f3 ('Don't forget to precompile the embed css') added 'embed.css' to config.assets.precompile, and 5621a645 moved embed.js from app/assets to public/javascripts so it is served statically without precompilation.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: 67e20416 replaced the per-URL throttle key with a global `retrieved_topic` 60s key; main's TopicRetriever is identical, so varying the query string no longer bypasses the throttle (at most one anonymous retrieval per minute site-wide). Distinct URLs still map to distinct topics, but not at an unbounded rate.

astra.pergunta: opa-01: 67e20416 (2016-11-16) changed the throttle key from retrieved:#{url} to a global retrieved_topic (60s). Confirmado or pendente?
astra.resposta: Confirmado 2016-11-16: the global key removes the query-string bypass; distinct topics over time do not reproduce it.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: The specs were rewritten on 2014-04-24 (#2428), but no example ever isolated feed_polling_enabled (the enabled=false example also left the URL nil). spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb and Jobs::PollFeed were deleted by #8233 when RSS polling moved to a plugin, without targeting the gap.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: TopicEmbed.import_remote fetches the embed URL with open(url).read and no timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge remote page can block the background job and exhaust memory.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: The open(url).read call was rewritten several times (2016 allow_redirections, 2020 FinalDestination, 2023-11-09 SSRF fix 5f20748e) and today TopicEmbed.find_remote does FinalDestination::HTTP.get_response(uri) then parse_html(response.body). FinalDestination::HTTP only overrides connect for SSRF filtering; no read/total timeout and no body-size cap are set, so the whole body is still read into memory with Net::HTTP defaults, as with open-uri in 2013. The changes targeted SSRF/redirects, not the unbounded fetch.

astra.pergunta: Fetch rewritten to FinalDestination::HTTP.get_response with no explicit timeout or size cap: confirmado, pendente or descontinuado?
astra.resposta: Default 60s timeouts bound each read, not total duration; body still fully loaded without size limit; security changes addressed SSRF/redirects only.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: TopicEmbed.find_remote on main does FinalDestination::HTTP.get_response(uri) and parse_html(response.body); FinalDestination::HTTP gained an opt-in total_timeout (unset by default, not set by find_remote) and there is still no body-size cap, so the unbounded fetch remains.

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: GET /embed/best?embed_url=http://<embeddable_host>/<any path>?x=<unique> with a Referer on the embeddable host (any non-browser client can set it), where the path trickles its body or is a large file | observed: ev/7 (open-uri over loopback): a trickling page held read for 12.1s, as long as the server chose, since read_timeout resets per chunk; a 150 MB page was read whole into one String | expected: the fetch aborts after a total deadline and above a size cap | topic_embed.rb:48 does open(url).read with no total timeout and no size limit, and it runs in the RetrieveTopic job enqueued from embed_controller.rb:15 (and in the Disqus importer). The only restriction is that the host equals embeddable_host (topic_retriever.rb:15). The path and query are free, so they bypass the per-URL throttle and can point at a slow or large resource such as a media file, tying up a worker and its memory. Upstream later added a total-deadline mechanism to FinalDestination::HTTP for this class of problem.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: An authorized embed request targets http://blog.example/large.html on the configured host, with polling disabled and a valid import author; the server returns a 3 GiB body to a worker with less available memory. | observed: The retrieval downloads the response without a size cap, then attempts to materialize the entire body as a Ruby string before Readability runs, exhausting the worker's available memory. | expected: Reject an oversized response while streaming it, before allocating the full body, and enforce a bounded retrieval duration. | app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 enqueues retrieval, app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17 invokes TopicRetriever, and lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 and :48-52 allow this configured-host URL through to import_remote. app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 calls open(url).read without a size limit. [Ruby 2.0 open-uri](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ruby/ruby/v2_0_0_353/lib/open-uri.rb) buffers large downloads in a temporary file, but the subsequent unrestricted read still creates the full in-memory string. The blanket claim of no timeout needs qualification: [Net::HTTP has a 60-second per-read timeout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ruby/ruby/v2_0_0_353/lib/net/http.rb), which supplies neither a total deadline nor a body-size limit.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The retrieve throttle sets the Redis key with setnx and sets its TTL in a separate expire call, so a crash between the two leaves a key without expiry that blocks retrieval of that URL forever.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: lib/topic_retriever.rb on main still does `if Discourse.redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `Discourse.redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. Later commits only renamed $redis to Discourse.redis (2019) and changed the key to a global "retrieved_topic" (67e20416, 2016), so a crash between the two commands still leaves a key without TTL that blocks retrieval (now for all URLs).
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: lib/topic_retriever.rb on main still does `if Discourse.redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then a separate `Discourse.redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`; only the redis handle and key name changed.

evidenciaV4.opus: The trigger is still a worker that dies in the gap between two back-to-back Redis calls (topic_retriever.rb:27-28). No request input can cause that, and an ordinary deploy restart is very unlikely to land in a window that small. Even in that state the article is not blocked for everyone: any staff view bypasses the throttle (retrieve_topic.rb:17, topic_retriever.rb:23) and imports it, after which TopicEmbed exists and every viewer gets the topic. Using SET NX EX would be cleaner, but this is a robustness nit that depends on fault injection, not a defect reached by a realistic input, so I keep FP.
evidenciaV4.astra: Keep TP (bug; no subclass). An ordinary anonymous retrieval reaches the separate SETNX and EXPIRE calls in topic_retriever.rb:27–28; process termination between them leaves a permanent throttle key. With feed polling disabled, subsequent anonymous requests never retry fetching, leaving the embed loading indefinitely. A staff bypass is a manual workaround, and operational process termination need not be caused by request input for this failure to be real.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: `import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: The open-uri fetch persisted through rewrites (2017: open(url, allow_redirections: :safe).read; later uri.read). Commit da839e6 (2020-05-27, 'SECURITY: Use FinalDestination for topic embeds') added FinalDestination resolution with validate_uri, validating each redirect hop, but still fetched the resolved URL with open-uri following redirects without IP checks. Commit 5f20748 'SECURITY: SSRF vulnerability in TopicEmbed - Block redirects when making the final request' (authored 2023-10-27, landed on main via PR #24304 merged 2023-11-09) replaced it with FinalDestination::HTTP.get plus DisallowedIpError, closing the redirect-follow SSRF; main today still uses FinalDestination + FinalDestination::HTTP.get_response.

astra.pergunta: Which change fixes the bug: 2020 FinalDestination resolve (validates hops, but final fetch still open-uri following redirects) or 2023 commit blocking redirects on the final fetch?
astra.resposta: The 2023 commit 5f20748: the 2020 change blocks the plain redirect chain during resolution but the actual fetch still follows redirects without IP validation; 2023 disables redirects on the fetch and applies IP checks.
astra.veredito: confirmado, fix = 5f20748 / PR #24304 (2023-11-09); 2020 da839e6 noted as partial mitigation.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: PostMover#copy recreates the first post via PostCreator without passing cook_method, so a moved raw_html (embedded/imported) first post is re-cooked through the markdown pipeline and its content changes.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: At the benchmark head PostMover#copy called PostCreator.create with only raw/topic_id/acting_user. Blame of today's app/models/post_mover.rb shows `cook_method: post.cook_method` in create_first_post was added by commit b3094e9954 (PR #5360, 'FIX: incoming and outgoing emails got lost when post was moved'), whose diff adds cook_method, via_email and raw_email to the PostCreator options. Today the first-post copy preserves cook_method.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: EmbedController#best renders the 'loading' placeholder and still calls discourse_expires_in 1.minute, so the anonymous cache stores the placeholder under the embed URL and visitors keep seeing 'Loading Discussion...' for up to a minute after the topic exists.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: From 2013-12-31 the embed action (best, later comments) kept a trailing `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` after both branches, so the loading placeholder was cached. PR #44101 (2026-10-07, 'Render embedded comments without the 30 second refresh delay') moved `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` into the topic branch and sets `Cache-Control: no-cache` before `render "loading"`; its message states the loading page is no longer cached. Main today has that shape.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: TopicEmbed.import wraps PostCreator#create in Topic.transaction, so PostCreator's post-transaction job enqueueing (process_post, feature_topic_users, etc.) runs before the outer transaction commits, and a worker that picks up ProcessPost early finds no post and skips post-processing for the imported topic.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: TopicEmbed.import still wraps PostCreator.create in Topic.transaction on main, but PR #11293 (2020-12-08, 'Always enqueue sidekiq jobs after database transaction commit') changed Jobs.enqueue (app/jobs/base.rb) to push via `DB.after_commit`, which hooks the outermost ActiveRecord transaction. So ProcessPost and the other PostCreator jobs are no longer enqueued before the outer Topic.transaction commits; the buggy ordering is fixed generically.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The migration adds posts.cook_method with a default and NOT NULL in one add_column, which on the PostgreSQL versions of the time rewrites the whole posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and blocks reads and writes during deploy.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb still exists on main with the identical `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`; its only later commits are the Migration[4.2] and frozen_string_literal edits. No upstream change altered the column-add strategy. The impact is moot today (migration ran once on existing sites; current Discourse requires PostgreSQL 13+, where a constant default does not rewrite the table), but the code is unchanged.

astra.pergunta: Code unchanged but PG13+ makes the rewrite moot and the migration runs once: pendente or descontinuado?
astra.resposta: Descontinuado: behaviour no longer occurs on supported PG versions; not confirmado since no fix.

astra.pergunta: The rule's descontinuado requires code removed or rewritten; here only the environment changed. Strictly, pendente?
astra.resposta: Yes: code carrying the bug is still present and unchanged; loss of impact in current environment is neither a fix nor a removal.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb on main still has `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`; later commits were only Migration[4.2]/frozen_string_literal edits.

evidenciaV4.opus: We agree that PostgreSQL 9.2 rewrites posts under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE for an ADD COLUMN with a non-null default. The head tree has 13 other migrations doing the same add_column :posts ... default ... null: false, so this is how the project writes migrations. The documented upgrade path stops the app first, and deploy.rb.sample is only a sample. It is a one-time lock during upgrade with no wrong result or data effect, and a reviewer would not flag it against the project's own convention, so I keep FP.
evidenciaV4.astra: Keep TP (perf; no subclass). The new migration adds cook_method with a non-null default, requiring a [table-and-index rewrite on supported PostgreSQL 9.2](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.2/sql-altertable.html) under a [lock blocking reads and writes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.2/explicit-locking.html). config/deploy.rb.sample runs migrations after deploy:update_code without first stopping the application, so a large existing posts table can cause prolonged request blocking. Similar older migrations do not make this newly introduced operation pre-existing or remove its availability impact.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: PollFeed fetches feed_polling_url with Kernel#open, so a setting value starting with '|' runs a shell command on the job server. Anyone who can edit site settings gets command execution.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: Commit 'FIX: add http:// to feed_polling_url if it's missing' prefixes any value not matching ^https?:// with 'http://' before open(@feed_url), so a '|cmd' value can no longer reach Kernel#open's pipe mode; Kernel#open was later replaced by FinalDestination+Excon (5f318a5241, 2017-12-05, #5311) and the job removed in #8233 (2019-11-12).

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: Post#cook returns self.raw for raw_html posts and ignores the text it is given. Callers that cook different text, such as add_topic_to_quotes.rake, store cooked output that does not match the new raw.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: 'FIX: postprocessing ignored cook method' changed Post#cook(*args) to cook(raw, opts = {}), so 'return raw if cook_method == raw_html' now returns the text passed in, not self.raw; main still has this form.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The embed layout writes the full request.referer into the page, and the page is anon-cached for a minute under a key without the referer. One embedding page's full URL, including query secrets, can be served to other visitors.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: The embed layout still prints request.referer (now as data-referer) and comments are cached 1 minute, but 'SECURITY: Partition anonymous cache keys by Referer for embed routes' adds a SHA-256 of HTTP_REFERER to the anon cache key for /embed/, so one page's referer is no longer served to another.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: EmbedController#best enqueues a RetrieveTopic job for every request with an unknown embed_url, before any host validation or throttle. Repeated or varied requests produce an unbounded stream of jobs.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: EmbedController#comments on main still calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) on every request for an unknown embed_url with no throttle or dedupe before enqueue (host validation via EmbeddableHost.url_allowed? was added before it; the Redis throttle is still inside TopicRetriever).

evidenciaV4.opus: [desk] input: Repeated GET /embed/best?embed_url=http://<embeddable_host>/post?x=<n> with a Referer on embeddable_host (needed to pass ensure_embeddable, embed_controller.rb:26), from a logged-in user or with varying query strings | observed: embed_controller.rb:10-15: topic_id nil -> one Jobs.enqueue per request; the job (retrieve_topic.rb) runs TopicRetriever#retrieve, where invalid_host? (topic_retriever.rb:14-19) and the per-URL redis setnx (21-33) reject repeats with O(1) work. Anonymous identical requests, including the 30 s reload in loading.html.erb, are served from the 1-minute anon cache (embed_controller.rb:19, anonymous_cache.rb:14) and do not reach the controller. | expected: At most one cheap job per request; the expensive work (feed poll / remote fetch) bounded per URL | The trace shows exactly one enqueue per request that reaches the controller, and that job does a constant, cheap check before bailing (topic_retriever.rb:9, 27). Work is linear in request rate like any endpoint, and moving the throttle before the enqueue would not stop distinct query-string variants (each has its own key). No wrong result or meaningful amplification is shown, so this is a hardening suggestion, not a defect.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: Production defaults, embeddable_host='blog.example', embed_by_username unset; anonymous GET /embed/best?embed_url=https%3A%2F%2Fblog.example%2Farticle with Referer https://blog.example/article, repeated after 30 seconds. | observed: The first request enqueues a job, which cannot import without a configured user. The 30-second reload receives the cached loading page; distinct query strings can enqueue additional jobs, but this does not establish an accumulating backlog or meaningful performance failure. | expected: Retry unresolved imports while throttling retrieval; no concrete incorrect result is demonstrated by this trace. | The request passes Referer validation at app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:25-26 and enqueues at :15; the worker reaches lib/topic_retriever.rb:49-50 and returns without importing. However, app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 and app/controllers/application_controller.rb:170 enable one-minute caching, so lib/middleware/anonymous_cache.rb:83 serves the reload without another enqueue. Query variants bypass the cache key at lib/middleware/anonymous_cache.rb:14, but worker-side host rejection and retrieval throttling still apply at lib/topic_retriever.rb:9. Additional enqueue operations alone do not demonstrate the claimed meaningful queue-growth defect; under the requested standard, this is FP.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: TopicEmbed.import checks post.present? after PostCreator#create, but PostCreator returns an unsaved post when it rolls back on host spam. TopicEmbed.create! then runs with nil ids and raises, which aborts the import.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: Commit 'Updated import for TypePad' added 'return if @opts[:skip_validations]' to PostCreator#rollback_if_host_spam_detected; TopicEmbed.import passes skip_validations: true, so the host-spam rollback that left an unsaved post no longer happens (today PostCreator#valid? still returns true before has_host_spam? when skip_validations, and the TopicEmbed is created inside PostCreator).

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: absolutize_urls leaves out the port when it is 80 or 443 regardless of scheme, so relative links in content from http://host:443 or https://host:80 are rewritten to the wrong port.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reasonUpstreamV4: app/models/topic_embed.rb absolutize_urls on main still has 'prefix += ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443', unchanged in the way that matters.

enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.prTitle: Enhanced Pagination Performance for High-Volume Audit Logs

prOriginal.nota: No original upstream PR: head 8ab88145 is a synthetic benchmark commit (bobharper208, 2025-07-25) on upstream 74618671; gh search prs for the title and for OptimizedCursorPaginator returned nothing, and the commit history of both touched files upstream contains none of its code.

enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.bug: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.reason: The benchmark head 8ab88145 is a synthetic commit (author bobharper208, Claude-generated message) on top of upstream 74618671; no upstream PR matches its title, and upstream paginator.py / organization_auditlogs.py history since 2025-05 never contains OptimizedCursorPaginator, optimized_pagination or enable_advanced_features. The OptimizedCursorPaginator negative-slice branch never existed on upstream master; today's paginator.py has no such class.

enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.bug: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.reason: The benchmark head 8ab88145 is a synthetic commit (author bobharper208, Claude-generated message) on top of upstream 74618671; no upstream PR matches its title, and upstream paginator.py / organization_auditlogs.py history since 2025-05 never contains OptimizedCursorPaginator, optimized_pagination or enable_advanced_features. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key with math.floor on datetime never reached upstream; the audit-log endpoint upstream still uses DateTimePaginator only.

enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.bug: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.reason: The benchmark head 8ab88145 is a synthetic commit (author bobharper208, Claude-generated message) on top of upstream 74618671; no upstream PR matches its title, and upstream paginator.py / organization_auditlogs.py history since 2025-05 never contains OptimizedCursorPaginator, optimized_pagination or enable_advanced_features. The unconditional organization_context.member.has_global_access dereference was added only by the synthetic commit; upstream organization_auditlogs.py (later moved to core in #97407) never had it.

enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.bug: A user-controlled optimized_pagination flag lets any member with global access switch to a paginator that accepts unvalidated negative cursor offsets, widening the attack surface and causing server errors.
enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.reason: The benchmark head 8ab88145 is a synthetic commit (author bobharper208, Claude-generated message) on top of upstream 74618671; no upstream PR matches its title, and upstream paginator.py / organization_auditlogs.py history since 2025-05 never contains OptimizedCursorPaginator, optimized_pagination or enable_advanced_features. The request-controlled optimized_pagination flag never existed upstream, so the widened surface was never shipped.

enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.bug: BasePaginator.get_result clamps negative offsets only for next cursors; a prev cursor with a negative offset is passed straight into the queryset slice, which Django rejects with an error (500) on every paginated endpoint.
enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.reason: The benchmark head 8ab88145 is a synthetic commit (author bobharper208, Claude-generated message) on top of upstream 74618671; no upstream PR matches its title, and upstream paginator.py / organization_auditlogs.py history since 2025-05 never contains OptimizedCursorPaginator, optimized_pagination or enable_advanced_features. The partial clamp (max(0, offset) only for next cursors) and its 'safe' comment never reached upstream. Note: upstream BasePaginator.get_result today still slices queryset[offset:stop] with no negative-offset check in either direction (pre-existing behaviour; #122411 and #127885 added rejection only to GenericOffsetPaginator and OffsetPaginator), but that is not the benchmark-attributed change.

astra.pergunta: Negative-offset slicing in BasePaginator pre-existed upstream and is still there, but the benchmark PR (partial clamp + false comment) was never merged. nao_entrou_no_original or pendente?
astra.resposta: nao_entrou_no_original: the original PR was never merged and its partial clamp/comment never existed upstream; the pre-existing BasePaginator issue remaining unresolved does not show the benchmark-attributed bug reached upstream.

In an insecure context navigator.clipboard is undefined and the call throws synchronously before showToast, so no false success there either. Astra gives no concrete browser or configuration where the rejection happens on this click, so this stays an un-awaited-promise style nit; when in doubt, FP.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.prTitle: feat(uptime): Add ability to use queues to manage parallelism

prOriginal.nota: Found by title search (branch danf/uptime-queue-consumer). Benchmark head 9966ec5a is the PR's last commit; same 7 files. Squash-merged as 33f4fddf.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: Claims OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets requires every integer offset to exist, so Kafka offset gaps permanently block commits for the partition and per-partition state is never cleared on rebalance.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: #95753 added OffsetTracker.update_assignments()/clear(), called from SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.__init__ with the new partitions, so per-partition state is reset on every assignment. The gap scan in get_committable_offsets stayed unchanged (only one contiguous run per cycle), but the 'permanent block' was already overstated by both reviewers; the module was later deleted in #97340.

astra.pergunta: Did #95753 fix the reset-on-rebalance / gap-blocking behaviour, or did it survive until deletion?
astra.resposta: Confirmado, partially: #95753 resets tracking state on assignment changes; the gap algorithm is unchanged so the one-contiguous-run-per-cycle limitation survived; the permanent block was inaccurate.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: OrderedQueueWorker marks a work item's offset complete in a finally block even when processing raised, so failed messages are committed and dropped, contradicting the documented guarantee of committing only after successful processing.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: OrderedQueueWorker.run kept calling offset_tracker.complete_offset in the finally block after a processor exception in every later version (#95753, #95919, #95943 touched run() but not this). #97340 (2025-08-07) deleted queue_consumer.py, test_queue_consumer.py and the thread-queue-parallel tests/mode as unused code, not targeting this bug.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: The test test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling has a docstring that doesn't match the test implementation.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling kept its docstring and the 'no commit' assertion; later commits only added consumer_group='test' to the factory. #97340 (2025-08-07) deleted queue_consumer.py, test_queue_consumer.py and the thread-queue-parallel tests/mode as unused code, not targeting this bug.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: The error-handling test asserts no commit happened after only a 0.2s sleep while the commit loop runs every second, so it passes without ever observing whether a failed offset gets committed.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: The error-handling test kept the 0.2s sleep before asserting no commit while the commit interval stayed 1.0s by default; later commits only added consumer_group. #97340 (2025-08-07) deleted queue_consumer.py, test_queue_consumer.py and the thread-queue-parallel tests/mode as unused code, not targeting this bug.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: FixedQueuePool uses unbounded queues and the strategy never applies backpressure, so when workers fall behind the consumer keeps polling and queued work items grow memory without limit, contrary to the documented backpressure guarantee.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: FixedQueuePool kept creating queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit/poll never applied backpressure in #95753/#95919; the unbounded queues survived. #97340 (2025-08-07) deleted queue_consumer.py, test_queue_consumer.py and the thread-queue-parallel tests/mode as unused code, not targeting this bug.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: Graceful shutdown sets each worker's shutdown flag before draining, so workers stop with items still queued, and close() stops the commit thread first, so finished work is not committed and gets replayed.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: #95753 moved the commit thread into the pool and stopped close() from shutting down the pool, but FixedQueuePool.shutdown still sets worker.shutdown before draining, and the new join()/flush() discards queued work and clears the offset tracker without a final commit, so completed work could still be replayed. Behaviour survived in reshaped form until deletion. #97340 (2025-08-07) deleted queue_consumer.py, test_queue_consumer.py and the thread-queue-parallel tests/mode as unused code, not targeting this bug.

astra.pergunta: Did #95753 fix the shutdown drain / final-commit behaviour?
astra.resposta: Descontinuado: workers still get shutdown flags before draining; moving the commit thread does not guarantee a final commit; flush() clears tracking without committing completed work, so replay remains possible.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: The strategy's close() shuts down the factory-owned shared queue pool, so after a partition rebalance the next strategy reuses a dead pool; submissions fail and the error handler marks their offsets complete, committing messages that were never processed.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: #95753 ('Fix thread-queue-parallel consumer to handle Kafka rebalances correctly') removed queue_pool.shutdown() from SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/terminate/join, moved the commit thread to the factory-owned pool to survive rebalances, and added update_assignments, so a replacement strategy no longer reuses a dead pool.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: The strategy invokes Arroyo's commit callback from a background thread rather than from submit/poll on the consumer thread, so commits can race with polling and partition revocation on a non-thread-safe consumer.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: #95753 moved _commit_loop from the strategy into FixedQueuePool, but it still runs in a background daemon thread and calls Arroyo's commit callback outside submit/poll. #97340 (2025-08-07) deleted queue_consumer.py, test_queue_consumer.py and the thread-queue-parallel tests/mode as unused code, not targeting this bug.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: The tests named for concurrent processing across groups only check that all items were processed and all groups seen, so a fully serial implementation would pass and concurrency is never verified.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: test_concurrent_processing_across_groups and test_thread_queue_parallel_concurrent_subscriptions kept asserting only counts/groups seen (later changes only shortened timeouts and adjusted WorkItem/consumer_group). #97340 (2025-08-07) deleted queue_consumer.py, test_queue_consumer.py and the thread-queue-parallel tests/mode as unused code, not targeting this bug.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: The strategy ordering test submits identical messages and only checks the count processed, so it cannot detect out-of-order processing within a group.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: test_preserves_order_within_group kept submitting identical sub1 messages and asserting only len==5 (#95753 only changed the timeout). #97340 (2025-08-07) deleted queue_consumer.py, test_queue_consumer.py and the thread-queue-parallel tests/mode as unused code, not targeting this bug.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: The graceful-shutdown test only asserts that the factory cleared its queue_pool reference, which shutdown always does, so it does not verify that pending work is drained or workers stop.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown kept asserting only factory.queue_pool is None; later commits only added consumer_group. #97340 (2025-08-07) deleted queue_consumer.py, test_queue_consumer.py and the thread-queue-parallel tests/mode as unused code, not targeting this bug.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: The test's wait loop stops at the first recorded commit but asserts the committed offset is exactly 105, so a commit fired mid-processing can record a lower offset and make the test flaky.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_commit kept the wait loop that breaks on any commit and asserts offset 105; later commits only added consumer_group. #97340 (2025-08-07) deleted queue_consumer.py, test_queue_consumer.py and the thread-queue-parallel tests/mode as unused code, not targeting this bug.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: The per-worker queue_depth gauge is tagged only with identifier, so all queues report into one series and the metric shows whichever queue reported last.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: The remote_subscriptions.queue_worker.queue_depth gauge kept only the identifier tag in all later versions (#95943 added a processing_time timer with the same single tag). #97340 (2025-08-07) deleted queue_consumer.py, test_queue_consumer.py and the thread-queue-parallel tests/mode as unused code, not targeting this bug.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.terminate signals the commit thread without joining it, so the background thread is claimed to keep committing offsets for revoked partitions after terminate.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: PR #95753 'Fix thread-queue-parallel consumer to handle Kafka rebalances correctly' states the commit thread kept running after partition revocation and committed offsets for partitions no longer owned. It moved the commit thread from SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy into FixedQueuePool (joined on shutdown), added a shutdown recheck after wait(), and resets the offset tracker on revocation; terminate() no longer owns a commit thread. The whole thread-queue-parallel mode and queue_consumer.py were later removed (e6ab8605, 2025-08-07, #97340).

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.bug: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy passes FilteredPayload to decode_payload, whose assert raises instead of returning None, so filtered messages go through the error path.
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.reason: Between the merge and 2025-08-07, upstream changes to queue_consumer.py (#95753, #95919, #95942, #95943) left SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit the same where it matters: it still calls decoder(message.payload) (decode_payload asserts not FilteredPayload) before the None check, and the except fallback only completes offsets when message.value is a BrokerValue. So filtered DLQ-stale messages kept leaving their offsets uncommitted. PR #97340 ('Remove thread-queue-parallel mode and related code', 2025-08-07) deleted queue_consumer.py and the thread-queue-parallel wiring in result_consumer.py and consumers/__init__.py, saying the mode was unused and had not helped much. It did not target this bug. Today's master has no queue mode; decode_payload still asserts, but only the serial, parallel and batched-parallel modes remain.
