feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.bug: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.reason: Commit 07d6bb8d 'FIX: remove client side maximum filesize check' deleted the hard-coded maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 check from validateUploadedFile, leaving the per-type limits to the server. The remaining hard-coded value in the 413 handler was replaced by Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] in a5d8dfb0 (2016-04-06, 'FIX: don't hardcode maximum file size').

feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.bug: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.reason: Commit d541018b 'FIX: automagic image downsizing wasn't working for GIFs...' replaced the "80%" argument with dimensions computed from FastImage as "#{(w * 0.8).floor}x#{(h * 0.8).floor}", i.e. WxH geometry that gifsicle --resize-fit accepts.

feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.bug: Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.
feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.reason: Commit a3831a70 'FIX: uploading an animated user card/profile background was converted to a still image' made the controller pass filename: filename to OptimizedImage.downsize and changed optimize to pick the _animated branch when from =~ /\.GIF$/i || opts[:filename] =~ /\.GIF$/i, so an extensionless multipart tempfile of a GIF now takes the animated path.

feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.bug: Claims up to five synchronous ImageMagick runs per oversized upload block request threads and enable DoS.
feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.reason: The loop was reduced to 2 attempts (d541018b, 2015-11-09) and later moved to UploadCreator#downsize!, which today still runs up to 3 synchronous OptimizedImage.downsize (ImageMagick) passes per oversized image. The controller now wraps create_upload in hijack, which schedules it via Scheduler::Defer in the same web process, so the in-process multi-pass conversion remains, only mitigated.

astra.pergunta: Given benchmark loop of 5 synchronous downsizes (inside Scheduler::Defer or synchronous API), and today's hijack -> Scheduler::Defer + UploadCreator#downsize! with 3.times and early exits, which status applies?
astra.resposta: Multiple synchronous ImageMagick passes remain (up to three); upload runs through hijack/Scheduler::Defer in a defer thread of the same web-worker process; reductions and hijack mitigate but do not eliminate the pattern.

feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.reasonUpstreamV4: On discourse/discourse main today, lib/upload_creator.rb UploadCreator#downsize! still runs up to 3 synchronous OptimizedImage.downsize passes (scale 0.5) per oversized image inside the upload request/hijack flow; no later commit to that file (latest 2026-11-13) removes the in-process multi-pass downsizing.

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: Logged-in user uploads a composer image of 10 MB (the new client-side cap, utilities.js:182) with max_image_size_kb=3072, via the default non-API path; plus a worst case where convert does not shrink the file. | observed: ev/1/main.rb (exact head loop, stubbed downsize at 80%x80% => ~0.64x size): 10MB jpeg -> 3 convert passes, final 2684 KB; 4MB -> 1 pass; non-shrinking/failing convert -> 5 passes then stops. | expected: Oversized image reduced below the limit with bounded work; that is what happens. No unbounded or attacker-amplified work. | The loop (app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-69) is hard-capped at 5 passes on a file the client caps at 10 MB, and the default path runs it in Scheduler::Defer.later (uploads_controller.rb:19-23) after render, so the request returns immediately (Unicorn drains it after the response, lib/scheduler/defer.rb:83-87). Upload.create_for already ran synchronous convert/ImageOptim on every image before this PR (app/models/upload.rb:69,98-102), so the PR adds a bounded constant factor to existing per-upload work by an authenticated user, not a demonstrable DoS. Upstream kept the same design for 11 years (now 3 passes). This is a design preference, not a defect worth a review comment.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: Authenticated POST /uploads with type=composer, a valid 4 MiB photo.png, default max_image_size_kb=3072, and no synchronous API flag. | observed: The controller queues processing and returns success. Processing performs at most five downsizing attempts, stopping once the file meets the limit; this trace does not establish request-worker exhaustion. | expected: Process the oversized image and apply the upload size limit; no demonstrated incorrect outcome requires a change. | Ordinary uploads use Scheduler::Defer and return immediately (app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:19-23); the bounded loop calls synchronous conversion at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-68 and app/models/optimized_image.rb:160-164. Unicorn does drain deferred work on its request worker (lib/scheduler/defer.rb:83-87), so deferral alone does not eliminate processing costs. However, upload processing already performed synchronous conversion and optimization before this PR (app/models/upload.rb:69,98-102), and this input establishes additional bounded work, not the claimed easy DoS. Without a concrete trace demonstrating meaningful exhaustion introduced by these passes, the claim does not meet the requested TP standard.

feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.bug: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.reason: Five days after the feature, commit 827ea641 'FIX: Use File.size instead of IO.size' replaced tempfile.size with File.size(tempfile.path) in the loop condition and in the filesize passed to Upload.create_for, so the size is re-read from the path after ImageOptim replaces the file.

feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.bug: The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.
feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.reason: Commit a5d8dfb0 'FIX: don't hardcode maximum file size' replaced var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 in the 413 case with Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] and made the max size settings client-visible again.

feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.bug: The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.reason: Commit 15b5fddd 'SECURITY: protect upload params, only allow very strict filenames' added raise Discourse::InvalidAccess unless type =~ /^[a-z\-\_]{1,100}$/ in UploadsController#create and OptimizedImage.ensure_safe_paths! (only [_\-a-zA-Z0-9./]) in every *_instructions method, including downsize_instructions. Shell metacharacters can no longer reach the backtick command.

feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.bug: Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.
feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.reason: The controller downsize loop was gated by Upload.should_optimize?(tempfile.path) since 2016-02-22 (4d981cec), which still let SVG through. Commit 5e2545a5 'FEATURE: improve support for (whitelisted) SVGs as images' changed it to `return false if path =~ /\.(gif|svg)$/i` (comment: don't optimize GIFs or SVGs); Rack 1.6.4 multipart tempfiles keep the extension, so oversized SVGs stop being downsized. Today UploadCreator routes :svg to clean_svg! and never to downsize!.

astra.pergunta: Is 5e2545a5 (should_optimize? excludes .svg by tempfile path) the fix, given Rack 1.6.4 tempfile naming, or the 2017 UploadCreator refactor?
astra.resposta: Rack 1.6.4 keeps the original extension in the multipart tempfile, so the new guard excludes SVGs; the 2017 refactor only made it explicit by type.

feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.bug: The oversized-image downsize loop in UploadsController#create always uses allow_animated_thumbnails as the animation policy, so with allow_animated_avatars on and allow_animated_thumbnails off an oversized animated GIF avatar is reduced to its first frame before Upload.create_for applies the avatar setting, losing the animation.
feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.reasonUpstreamV4: Commit a3831a7 ('FIX: uploading an animated user card/profile background was converted to a still image', pushed directly, no PR) changed the controller's downsize loop to `allow_animation = type == "avatar" ? SiteSetting.allow_animated_avatars : SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`, so avatars now use the avatar animation policy before Upload.create_for.

feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.bug: Each iteration of the downsize retry loop in UploadsController#create runs a full ImageOptim pass via convert_with, and Upload.create_for optimizes the result again, so a single oversized upload can trigger up to six expensive optimization runs inside the request.
feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.reasonUpstreamV4: The loop moved from UploadsController to UploadCreator#downsize! (9641d24, 2017-05-10) and is capped at 3 passes, but each pass still calls OptimizedImage.downsize -> optimize -> optimize_image (FileHelper.optimize_image!) on the intermediate file (app/models/optimized_image.rb:448-473 on main), and UploadCreator also runs optimize! once; the per-pass optimization pattern is still there.

evidenciaV4.opus: [desk] input: A ~10 MB JPEG photo uploaded via UploadsController#create with max_image_size_kb = 3072 | observed: Trace at ffbaf8c: uploads_controller.rb:64 condition true; loop at :66-69 calls OptimizedImage.downsize(path,path,'80%') -> optimized_image.rb optimize -> convert_with runs convert then ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to) (:163); the file shrinks to roughly 64% area per pass, so ~3 passes (10 -> ~6.4 -> ~4.1 -> ~2.6 MB) each with an ImageOptim run, then Upload.create_for runs ImageOptim again (upload.rb:102). Result: the correct, downsized and optimized image; only extra CPU time. Five passes need an image that stays above the limit after shrinking to ~10% of its area. | expected: Same output image; at most a cheaper pipeline that optimizes once at the end. | The behaviour is correct: every upload ends downsized and optimized, and the intermediate ImageOptim pass is not pure waste, since the loop's exit test is the file size (uploads_controller.rb:66) and optimizing each pass helps it get under max_image_size_kb in fewer resizes. What is left is an efficiency trade-off that only matters in rare extreme cases, and upstream has kept the same per-pass optimize design for 11 years (UploadCreator#downsize! today). Nothing shows wrong behaviour, so it counts as FP when in doubt.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: Authenticated multipart upload with type=composer, file=spec/fixtures/images/logo.png (2,297 bytes), and max_image_size_kb=1. | observed: The image enters the resize loop. Each successful conversion invokes ImageOptim before the next size check; Upload.create_for invokes it again afterward. This establishes repeated optimization, but no incorrect result or demonstrated material slowdown. | expected: Check the optimized image size after resizing, stop when it fits or the retry limit is reached, and validate the resulting upload. | The multipart file reaches the bounded loop through app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:58-67; downsize delegates through app/models/optimized_image.rb:149-157 to optimization at :164. That optimization affects the next filesize check at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66, so intermediate passes can prevent unnecessary further shrinking. The additional optimization at app/models/upload.rb:102 is real, but invocation counts alone do not establish a meaningful performance defect. No concrete input was shown to cause wrong behavior or material performance harm, so this does not meet the requested TP threshold.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.prTitle: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding

prOriginal.nota: No upstream PR: the benchmark head d1c69189 is itself a direct commit by Robin Ward on discourse/discourse main (committer date 2015-08-20, no associated pull request; gh pr search by title finds nothing), and it is an ancestor of main. The reference date is that commit's date.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: app/models/embeddable_host.rb on main still has 'before_validation do host.sub!(%r{\Ahttps?://}, ""); host.sub!(%r{/.*\z}, "") end' with no nil guard, and Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host still assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] directly. Later commits only reformatted the regexes (\A/\z, RedundantSelf); a request without host still raises NoMethodError.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reasonUpstreamV4: discourse/discourse main app/models/embeddable_host.rb still runs host.sub!(%r{\Ahttps?://}, "") / host.sub!(%r{/.*\z}, "") in before_validation with no nil guard, and save_host still assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] directly; later commits only restyled the regexes.

evidenciaV4.opus: Astra's trace matches mine (ev/1 reproduces the NoMethodError at embeddable_host.rb:6), but it rests on the same input: a hand-built staff request with the host key left out. The only production client, embeddable-host.js.es6, will not save while buffered.host is empty. The controller already returns a 500 for other malformed staff payloads (a missing params[:embeddable_host] raises at embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23 the same way), so this is a 500-instead-of-422 nit on an admin-only endpoint and no realistic user hits it.
evidenciaV4.astra: Change to FP: the callback can crash on nil, but the production component blocks empty hosts through cantSave and the save guard. The supplied reproduction requires a handcrafted malformed request; no normal caller producing nil was established.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: On main, Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy still do EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then call save_host(host, :update) / host.destroy without a nil check or find/raise. The controller gained tags, user and staff logging but the lookups are unchanged, so an unknown id still yields NoMethodError (500).
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reasonUpstreamV4: On main, Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy still do EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and call save_host(host, :update) / host.destroy with no nil check.

evidenciaV4.opus: I concede. The two-tab stale delete or update is ordinary admin use, and ev/2 shows it reaching nil.destroy at embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:16 (and nil.host= at :23 for update). The result is an unhandled NoMethodError that comes back as a 500 and gets logged as an exception. The rubric counts missing error handling that surfaces as a failure as a defect, even if the frontend shows a 404 the same way. The actions are new in this PR.
evidenciaV4.astra: Keep TP (bug): two admin tabs can retain the same record ID, and deleting it in one makes update or deletion in the other dereference nil. These newly introduced actions therefore raise an unhandled exception during ordinary use. Similar frontend handling of 404 and 500 does not make missing server-side error handling correct.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: record_for_host became record_for_url and still runs where("lower(host) = ?", host) without lowercasing the bound value. Since PR #17840 (2022-08-09, onebox URL normalization) UrlHelper.normalized_encode downcases the host when the URL parses with ::URI, which covers ordinary ASCII URLs, but URLs that fall back to Addressable (e.g. non-ASCII path) keep the host's case, so the mismatch is only partly gone.

astra.pergunta: Lookup still compares lower(host) to an un-lowercased URI host; #17840 made normalized_encode downcase the host on the ::URI path, with an Addressable fallback. Confirmado, pendente or descontinuado?
astra.resposta: #17840 is a partial fix: the Addressable fallback keeps ASCII host case (IDNA only for non-ASCII hosts), e.g. https://ExAmPlE.com/café still binds ExAmPlE.com; its onebox motivation would not prevent counting it as a fix if it removed the behaviour.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reasonUpstreamV4: record_for_host became record_for_url and still runs where("lower(host) = ?", host) without downcasing the bound value; since 2022 UrlHelper.normalized_encode downcases the host when ::URI parses the URL, but the Addressable fallback keeps the case, so the code itself is unchanged.

evidenciaV4.opus: I concede. The validation regex at embeddable_host.rb:2 is /i and before_validation does not downcase, so a host saved as 'Example.com' is stored with its case. TopicRetriever (topic_retriever.rb:16) passes the site owner's discourseEmbedUrl unchanged, and record_for_host lowercases only the column (:17). So 'https://Example.com/article' compares 'example.com' to 'Example.com' and is rejected, while base h == host accepted it. The one-sided lower() is new code that does not do the case-insensitive match it was written for, with a concrete effect: the embed is not retrieved.
evidenciaV4.astra: Keep TP (bug), replacing my earlier Referer example: public/javascripts/embed.js preserves case in discourseEmbedUrl, which reaches TopicRetriever unchanged. Configure www.example.com and Example.com, then embed https://Example.com/article from a page on www.example.com: the lowercase browser Referer passes both versions, but retrieval passes only the base matcher. A local Ruby check confirmed those matching results. Thus normal embed configuration can expose the regression without a handcrafted Referer.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: Two days after the merge, commit d418c4cf (2015-08-22, 'FIX: Bug with migrating old embeddedable hosts with http://') added migration FixMigratedHosts that strips ^https?:// from embeddable_hosts.host, which fixes migrated hosts with a scheme. Nothing ever stripped path segments from migrated rows, and the original migration still inserts the lines verbatim, so migrated hosts with a path still never match URI.host; partial fix only.

astra.pergunta: d418c4cf strips only the scheme from migrated hosts, not paths. Confirmado or pendente?
astra.resposta: Partial fix: example.com/path stays unmatched; the bug explicitly includes path segments, so being uncommon does not remove the residual case. Would be confirmado if the report were scheme-only.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reasonUpstreamV4: Two days after the merge, commit d418c4cf 'FIX: Bug with migrating old embeddedable hosts with http://' added migration FixMigratedHosts (UPDATE embeddable_hosts SET host = regexp_replace(host, '^https?://', '', 'i')), fixing exactly the migrated-with-scheme case the base supported and tested (site_setting_spec 'works with a http host'). Path segments were never a documented legacy format ('Hostname only, do not begin with http://') and were not matched by the base either for schemeless entries, so the remaining edge is not the behaviour reported.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb on main still executes "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)" with each legacy host interpolated unescaped. Later commits on the file (Rails 5 fixes, formatting, the 2026 uncategorized guard) left the interpolation as is.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reasonUpstreamV4: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb on main still executes the INSERT with VALUES ('#{h}', ...) interpolated unescaped; later commits only reformatted the file and guarded category lookups.

evidenciaV4.opus: I accept that base stores URLs with paths: embed_controller_spec.rb:70 sets embeddable_hosts to include https://example.com/1234 (the 'host with a path' test at :87 varies only the referer). That widens the input contract to URLs, but the failure still needs an apostrophe inside an entry in an admin-only host allow-list, and the base example and every realistic entry (hostnames, or URLs like /1234) migrate cleanly per ev/5. The golden claim is an SQL injection in the controller; the controller has no such SQL, and the migration's only source is trusted admin data read once at upgrade, so no untrusted party can inject anything. A legal but contrived o'brien-style entry is not a realistic input, and when in doubt the verdict is FP.
evidenciaV4.astra: Keep TP (data): the base explicitly tests a stored URL with a path in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, including “works with a host with a path,” so hostname-only documentation does not establish the actual input contract. The legacy editor accepts a pasted URL such as https://example.com/author/o'brien, and the base matcher extracts its host successfully. The new migration interpolates that persisted value unescaped at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25, causing an upgrade-blocking SQL syntax error. The original report mislocates the SQL and does not establish an untrusted-attacker exploit, but the underlying quoting defect affects a realistic, previously working configuration.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: Fourteen minutes after the feature commit, Robin Ward pushed 676416f4 'FIX: Build broken when someone didn't have an embed category', which keeps category_id = 0 and only reads category_row[0]['id'] if category_row.cmd_tuples > 0, falling back to uncategorized_category_id. Main still has that guard (and since #39971 also guards the uncategorized lookup).

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: The post-save overwrite with Category.findById(categoryId) survived #14517 (2021, which only set the initial category with an uncategorized fallback) and #26374. PR #26420 bound the chooser to this.category, saved props.category_id = this.category.id and deleted the findById(this.categoryId) line, so a new host keeps the uncategorized category initialised in init after saving; #30122 (2025) later moved editing to a separate form page.

astra.pergunta: Overwrite with findById(categoryId) after save removed in #26420 (DEV refactor of CategoryChooser); #14517 only fixed initial render; #30122 later rewrote the UI. Confirmado or descontinuado?
astra.resposta: #14517 kept the line that cleared the category after saving; #26420 resolved the described behaviour even though tagged DEV; the later #30122 rewrite does not make it descontinuado since it was already fixed.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: Commit bf9626d0 'FIX: Embedding was broken with non-english URLs and ports' added 'host << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port.present? && uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443' in record_for_url before the lookup, so a stored host:port now matches. The line is still on main and spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb has an 'it works with ports' case.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: The 2-5 letter TLD limit in EmbeddableHost's host regex was widened in steps: 436da215ae (2015-12-15, 'allow .network') to {2,7}, then PR #4816 (2017-04-15, 'increase host_must_be_valid regex for .technology TLD') to {2,10}, which is the first change that accepts the bug's example example.technology; PR #7948 (2019-07-26) raised it to {2,24}. Today's main still has `\.[a-z]{2,24}` in host_must_be_valid. Fix date taken as #4816 because it makes the cited case pass; the partial widening started 2015-12-15.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: The embeddable-host component's delete action has no .catch(popupAjaxError) on destroyRecord(), so a failed host deletion is silently swallowed and the row stays with no feedback to the admin.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reasonUpstreamV4: Upstream main today has frontend/discourse/admin/components/embeddable-host.gjs whose delete() still does `this.host.destroyRecord().then(() => { this.args.deleteHost(this.host); })` inside dialog.confirm's didConfirm, with no catch/popupAjaxError.

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: Admin confirms delete of host row 'eviltrout.com'; DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/1 fails (500, e.g. the controller's host.destroy on nil after a concurrent delete, or network/session error), so destroyRecord() rejects. | observed: ev/1 (node:22-slim) running the exact delete() lines: rows=["eviltrout.com"] errorPopupShown=false unhandledRejections=["Error: DELETE ... -> 500"] | expected: The failure is shown to the admin via popupAjaxError, as save() does at line 40. | embeddable-host.js.es6:46-48 chains destroyRecord().then(...) with no rejection handler, while save() at :37-40 ends with .catch(popupAjaxError) (imported at :4). A failed DELETE leaves the row in place, the rejection is unhandled and the admin gets no feedback. Missing error handling that surfaces as a silent failure in a new UI introduced by this PR.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: Two admins load the same host row. One deletes it; the other confirms deletion of the now-stale row. | observed: The second DELETE fails, its promise rejects, and the stale row remains visible without an error dialog. | expected: Display the deletion failure so the admin knows the operation failed. | The second request finds no record and calls nil.destroy at app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:15-16. The request travels through app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:74-75, and the AJAX failure rejects at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/mixins/ajax.js:79. That rejection propagates through app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:125 to the success-only handler at app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46-48, so neither row removal nor an error popup runs. This new action has a concrete missing-error-feedback defect; the rejection is unhandled, rather than literally swallowed.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: The 'raises an error with a missing host' spec sends no referer, so the request fails on the nil referer regardless of the empty embeddable_hosts table; the missing-host behaviour is not actually tested.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reasonUpstreamV4: Upstream spec/requests/embed_controller_spec.rb on main still has `it "raises an error with a missing host"` doing only `get "/embed/comments", params: { embed_url: embed_url }` with no REFERER header and no host fabricated.

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: Spec 'raises an error with a missing host': embed_url given, no referer (nil), empty embeddable_hosts table. | observed: ev/2 (ruby:3.3-slim) with the exact record_for_host/host_allowed? lines: empty table + nil referer -> success=false; host PRESENT + nil referer -> success=false (spec still passes). The forked Surefire JVM ends with System.exit, so it can't hang, and neither of us has shown the leaked reader causing another test to fail. A missing finally that only matters on an already-failed path is test cleanup tidying (a nit) under RUBRICA, so FP.

Realm or admin-client teardown cannot stop this loop because it catches subsequent exceptions and continues. Eventual Surefire termination limits the leak’s lifetime but does not prevent resource consumption and interference with remaining tests; an already-failed test still needs bounded cleanup.

evidenciaV4.opus: Astra's path requires the started reader thread to not be scheduled once while the test thread completes 100 sequential admin REST DELETEs (GroupTest.java:151-153), each a full HTTP round trip to the Keycloak server; it names that ordering but gives no realistic input that produces it. My run (ev/) reproduced the exact thread/delete/assert structure with deletes costing 1-3 ms: 0/200 and 0/500 trials had zero reads overlapping the deletes (minimum ~92 overlapping reads), and still 0/200 under docker --cpus=0.2 on one throttled CPU; a non-overlapping run only appeared with zero-cost deletes, which 100 HTTP calls cannot be. evidenciaV4.astra: I change my verdict to FP. The added test starts the reader before performing 100 sequential HTTP DELETE requests; the claimed zero-read pass requires starving the reader throughout that entire workload. My earlier argument established only a theoretically permitted scheduling order, not a realistic execution, and the reported experiments provide evidence against it. Under the required realistic-trigger standard, the missing start latch does not establish this defect; the missing reader join is a separate concern.

fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.bug: Google createEvent selects the target calendar by credentialId only while the booking reference stores the destination's externalId; when two destination calendars share a credential the event is inserted into the first match but the reference records the other calendar, breaking later updates/deletes.
fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.reasonUpstreamV4: PR #11327 ('fix: Duplicate calendar events', 2023-09-14) keeps only the first google_calendar destination in createAllCalendarEvents, so two Google destinations sharing a credential are no longer both created and the credentialId lookup in Google createEvent resolves to that same first destination. PR #16622 (commit be77ac133c, 2025-03-02) then made Google createEvent use the passed externalCalendarId first (`externalCalendarId ?? ...find(credentialId)`), removing the mismatch outright.

fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.bug: In createAllCalendarEvents the no-credentialId branch runs per destination and reuses the organizer's credentials filtered by integration, so several same-integration destinations without credentialId create duplicate events on the organizer's calendar.
fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.reasonUpstreamV4: Duplicate events were targeted in steps: #11327 (2023-09-14) dedups Google destinations, #11668 (2023-10-03) uses only the first matching credential per destination, and #14617 ('Minimum fix for N Calendar Invites', 2024-04-16) sets eventCreated=true in the no-credentialId branch and breaks the loop, so same-integration destinations without credentialId no longer create repeated events.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.prTitle: FIX: proper handling of group memberships

prOriginal.nota: No upstream PR: the benchmark head 060cda77 (Régis Hanol, 'FIX: proper handling of group memberships') was committed directly to master on 2015-01-05 and is an ancestor of main (compare = ahead); /commits/<sha>/pulls is empty. The merged code is the benchmark head itself.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: The Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 totalPages moved unchanged from admin-group.js.es6 into components/group-members-input.js.es6 (7bfabb02, 2016-12-13). Commit 9090c7b0 'FIX: Admin groups editor was showing extra page when exactly 50 records' (2017-05-17) changed it to Math.ceil(userCount / limit).

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: The next/previous paging that set offset and called findMembers (which unconditionally setProperties from each response) survived unchanged, last in components/group-members-input rendered by admin/templates/group.hbs. No change ever added request cancellation or a staleness check; the admin group pages that rendered this paging were removed in c82b2dcc 'Remove admin group management pages' (2018-04-09), and the component itself was deleted as dead code in 352d43b1 (#8356, 2019-11-18), with findMembers rewritten to append-only load-more.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: Commit 8fd69fd3 'FIX: group member pages only showing first 50 members alphabetically' (2015-02-19) added a group/members controller with a loadMore action and a LoadMore view mixin on the public group members page, so members beyond the first 50 page are fetched by infinite scroll.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: Commit f7f5e39f 'FIX: Minor Admin bug with a setting when creating a new group' (2015-01-23) added group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present? to Admin::GroupsController#create.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: Commit e8323fa5 'FIX: removing a group from a user was not removing primary group' (2015-02-09) made remove_member load the user, set primary_group_id = nil when it equals the group id and save it, with a spec asserting primary_group_id becomes nil.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: PR #3378 'FIX: show error message if user already exist in group' (merged 2015-04-15) wrapped group.add in if !group.users.include?(user) and returns a 422 member_already_exist error instead of hitting the unique index (spec 'returns 422 if member already exists'). Earlier users in the list could still be added before the 422; that residue went away later when GroupsController#add_members began checking all users first (group.users.where(id: users.pluck(:id))) before adding any.

astra.pergunta: Does #3378 (skip-check returning 422 for an existing member, partial add still possible) count as the fix, or should the later all-or-nothing pre-check be the fix date?
astra.resposta: confirmado by 499bed69/#3378 on 2015-04-15: it directly fixed adding an existing member (no unique-index violation, 422 instead of 500); the partial add is a residual problem fixed later and does not delay the classification.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: GroupsController#members got a negative check in 982df3c1 'FIX: return status 400 for invalid member params' (2018-06-29: limit < 0 raises InvalidParameters) and an upper bound in 704c5795 'FIX: do not allow unbound membership lookups' (2019-06-17: limit > 1000 raises InvalidParameters). Main today uses fetch_limit_from_params(default:, max: MEMBERS_MAX_PAGE_SIZE). The fix date is when both halves were in place.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: The raw-id association delete survived 1c545d4c1e (2015-02-25, became group.users.delete(user.id)) and the move of remove_member from Admin::GroupsController to GroupsController in 6dd4bc7d57 (2015-11-10). PR #4592 'FEATURE: Group logs' (merged 2016-12-12) replaced group.users.delete(user.id) with group.remove(user), which destroys group_users where(user:) and is a no-op for a non-member, so the RecordNotFound path is gone. The change was made to add logging, not aimed at the bug; today remove_member delegates to GroupMemberRemover and the admin action no longer exists.

astra.pergunta: Status for the raw-id delete replaced incidentally by group.remove(user) in the Group logs PR?
astra.resposta: Confirmado via 05f55dbc10 (PR #4592, 2016-12-12): incidental fix counts.

astra.pergunta: The descontinuado definition covers rewrites that remove the behaviour without targeting the bug; does that apply?
astra.resposta: Yes, by the more specific definition the swap was a logic change not aimed at the bug; milestone 05f55dbc10, PR #4592, 2016-12-12.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: remove_member moved to GroupsController in 2015-11 (6dd4bc7d) still using group.users.delete. 79639e2d (2016-04-04) only added a daily Group.reset_all_counters job and resets in other admin actions, not in remove_member. Commit 05f55dbc ('FEATURE: Group logs', in PR #4592 'FEATURE: Public groups', 2016-12-12) replaced group.users.delete(user.id) with group.remove(user), which destroys GroupUser rows with callbacks so user_count is decremented; today removal goes through GroupManager.

astra.pergunta: Confirmado or descontinuado, and which change: 79639e2d (daily counter resync) or 05f55dbc (switch to group.remove)?
astra.resposta: 79639e2d only reconciles periodically, the wrong count persists between runs; 05f55dbc destroys GroupUser with callbacks and effectively fixes the behaviour even though it shipped inside a feature.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: The floor(user_count/limit)+1 totalPages formula survived in admin-group.js.es6 until 7bfabb029b (2016-12-13) moved the pagination verbatim into discourse/components/group-members-input.js.es6. Commit 9090c7b05b 'FIX: Admin groups editor was showing extra page when exactly 50 records' (2017-05-17, pushed directly, no PR) changed it to Math.ceil(userCount / limit), so at offset 50 of 100 members showingLast is true and Next no longer reaches an empty page.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: GroupsController#members now returns {members, meta} with pagination, but the public groups controller spec still expects a bare array and stays pending, so the new response contract is untested.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: After the merge the 'ensures that membership can be paginated' example in spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb stayed pending/skip (16156bdc1d changed pending to skip) and parsed the body as an array. Commit a2da2971af (PR #4594, 'FEATURE: Allow columns on group members page to be sortable') turned it into a running `it` and reads JSON.parse(response.body)["members"], so the {members, meta} pagination contract became tested.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: After removeMember succeeds, findMembers reloads with the old offset, clamped only by the stale user_count; removing the only member on the last page (e.g. 51 members, offset 50) requests offset equal to the new total and the admin sees an empty, out-of-range page.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reasonUpstreamV4: The page-based member paging (findMembers offset clamped by Math.min(user_count, offset), with previous/next actions, moved from the admin page into group-members-input in 7bfabb029b, 2016-12-13) survived until #8356 'FIX: Better handling of Group model state'. That refactor removed the clamp, the paging component and limit/offset page state, and replaced them with append-style loading plus a refresh flag. It targeted state leaking between the group card and the members page, not this bug. Today, group.ts removeMember calls reloadMembers(params, true), which resets the offset.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: Group#removeMember and #addMembers have no rejection handler and the admin controller discards their promises, so failed member additions/removals are silently swallowed with no error shown to the admin.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reasonUpstreamV4: PR #3378 'FIX: show error message if user already exist in group' (2015-04-15) added a .catch to Group#addMembers that alerts the server error. That was the reachable silent failure: at head, adding an existing member hits the unique index on group_users. Error handling moved to the controller as .catch(popupAjaxError) in 0442457e7b (2015-08-13) and is still there today (controllers/group/index.js). removeMember's promise is still not caught today, but at head its only server error (the automatic-group 422) cannot be triggered from the UI, because group_member.hbs hides the remove link for automatic groups.

prOriginal.nota: Found via gh pr list --search with the title; head 25bf964a is exactly the PR headRefOid (2 commits), merged via merge commit 57972d85 (closes #41242, #41008). Merged code matches the benchmark head.

fixing-re-authentication-with-passkeys-k.bug: PasswordForm now accepts passkey-only users, but only the keycloak.v2 login-password.ftl renders the passkeys conditional UI; the base template (used by the legacy keycloak theme) does not, so a passkey-only user is shown a password-only form they cannot complete.

The legacy keycloak login theme (parent=base) still has no login-password.ftl override, and neither the base template nor PasswordForm.java has a functional change since the merge (only an import-order commit a2c1055 on PasswordForm).
fixing-re-authentication-with-passkeys-k.reasonUpstreamV4: PR #52724 (commit 945216c398, 'Render every login page and the layout from the Base theme', merged 2026-11-10) rewrote base/login/login-password.ftl, which on main now imports passkeys.ftl and calls <@passkeys.conditionalUIData /> (lines 4, 18). So the base template now renders the passkeys UI for passkey-only users. Separately, PR #54388 removed the legacy 'keycloak' login theme on 2026-11-04.

UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled on main is unchanged (isPasskeysEnabled() && (user == null || isConfiguredFor(...))). The 2026-10-06 commit bf57c22456 added an assertion for a user whose passkey was removed, but that path renders via WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse/fillContextForm, not the per-user guard, and the named test was not changed.
fixing-re-authentication-with-passkeys-k.reasonUpstreamV4: On main, tests/webauthn/.../PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey still sets passkeysEnabled(false), and UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled (lines 169-172) is unchanged.

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled copied from the head, run for a user without a passkey under each test's realm config: passkeysEnabled=false (UsernamePasswordFormTest) and passkeysEnabled=true (UsernameFormTest), each against a mutant with the per-user guard removed | observed: passkeys off: head=false, mutant=false (indistinguishable); passkeys on: head=false, mutant=true (the guard decides the outcome) | expected: For this to be a defect, the per-user guard would have to go unverified, or the test would have to miss the behaviour it was written for. | The test's header comment (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:278) says it covers 'passkeys is not enabled for the realm', and with passkeysEnabled=FALSE (line 283) it does check that the webauth form is absent; only the inline comment at line 300 is misleading. This matches the configured scenario. | expected: With realm passkeys disabled, omit passkey controls and allow password re-authentication. | PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:278 explicitly identifies the intended scenario as re-authentication with realm passkeys disabled, and :283 configures it accordingly. No incorrect result follows from this input; the claim establishes a coverage distinction, not a defective test of its stated scenario. Additionally, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:346 enables realm passkeys and :359-360 checks absence for a user without a passkey, exercising the same inherited per-user guard through PasswordForm.java:52.

fixing-re-authentication-with-passkeys-k.bug: login-password.ftl now renders the passkeys macro, making reachable an error path where fillContextForm sets enableWebAuthnConditionalUI but returns before setting isUserIdentified/userVerification, so passkeys.ftl fails to render and a FreeMarker error replaces the login page.
fixing-re-authentication-with-passkeys-k.reason: PR #53554 'Passkeys conditional UI: HTTP 500 instead of login error page when an identified user has no passkey' (closes #52464) changed WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.fillContextForm to set ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI only when super.fillContextForm returns a non-null form, and removed the unconditional setAttribute from createErrorResponse. The passkeys macro is therefore no longer enabled without isUserIdentified/userVerification, and a test removing the server-side passkey now asserts the error page renders.

prOriginal.nota: Found via upstream commit history of src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py (843d7c7192, Alexander Tarasov). PR head branch fix/oauth-validate-github-integration-user has the same 5 commits ending at bb75657f; git diff bb75657f..843d7c71 on the 3 touched files is empty, so merged code equals the benchmark head.

github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.bug: OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value
github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.reason: The legacy OAuthLoginView was removed in #113338 (2026-04-20), but the logic moved to the API pipeline: _build_github_oauth_url still sends state=pipeline.signature and OAuthLoginApiStep.handle_post compares validated_data['state'] != pipeline.signature. pipeline/base.py still computes signature as md5 of the pipeline view class names, a constant per provider.
github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.reasonUpstreamV4: On master today, _build_github_oauth_url still sends state=pipeline.signature and OAuthLoginApiStep.handle_post rejects only when validated_data['state'] != pipeline.signature. Pipeline.signature is still the md5 of the view class names; none of the commits since 2024-04-04, including #128643 and #130934, changed this.

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: Two independent GitHub install pipelines (attacker and victim sessions). The attacker sends the victim to /extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker's OAuth code>&state=<attacker's observed state>&installation_id=<attacker's installation> | observed: ev/1 gives state 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3 for both pipelines (the same value the tests hardcode), and the victim's pipeline accepts the forged callback: True. | expected: Each attempt gets its own unpredictable state, stored in the pipeline session, so the victim's pipeline rejects a callback that carries another attempt's state. | integration.py:402 sends pipeline.signature as the OAuth state and :412 accepts any callback with that value. pipeline/base.py:132-133 builds it only from the view class names (integration.py:343-344), so it is the same for every user and every attempt. PipelineAdvancerView is csrf_protect=False and is reached with a plain GET, so an attacker can make the victim's pipeline bind the attacker's GitHub login and installation_id. The state check this PR adds against CSRF does not protect anything.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: A victim has an active GitHub setup pipeline. An attacker obtains an unused OAuth code for their own GitHub account and navigates the victim to /extensions/github/setup/?code=ATTACKER_CODE&state=9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3&installation_id=4242, where installation 4242 has sender.login matching the attacker and no organization association. | observed: The callback authenticates the attacker's GitHub account within the victim's pipeline and attaches installation 4242 to the victim's Sentry organization. | expected: Reject the callback because its OAuth authorization was not initiated by the victim's installation attempt. | src/sentry/pipeline/base.py:132-133 derives the signature exclusively from view class names, while src/sentry/web/frontend/pipeline_advancer.py:33-63 retrieves the victim's session pipeline and dispatches the callback without CSRF protection (line 27). src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:397-423 accepts the supplied installation ID and constant state, exchanges the attacker's code, and stores the returned attacker login at line 438. That login matches the attacker's installation metadata at lines 501-507, allowing completion through src/sentry/integrations/pipeline.py:93 and association with the victim's organization at lines 225-227.

github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.bug: The new OAuth step's token exchange and user lookup are not wrapped in error handling, so GitHub/network failures surface as 500s instead of the installation-failed page.
github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.reason: Today exchange_github_oauth calls safe_urlopen before the try that only guards safe_urlread/parse, and client.get_user_info() is unguarded; handle_post only catches GitHubPipelineError and organization_pipeline.py api_advance has no generic handler. Transport or HTTP errors still escape as 500 instead of the error result.
github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.reasonUpstreamV4: On master today, exchange_github_oauth calls safe_urlopen before the try, which guards only safe_urlread and the parsing, and client.get_user_info() is not guarded. handle_post catches only GitHubPipelineError, so transport and HTTP errors still escape.

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: GitHub's token endpoint is unreachable or times out (requests ConnectionError/Timeout), or GET api.github.com/user returns a non-2xx status (e.g. 502, or 401 for a revoked token). | observed: ev/2: a normal response gives next_step. When the token endpoint is down, ConnectionError is not handled, and a 502 from /user raises HTTPError that is not handled either. Both reach PipelineAdvancerView, which has no handler, so the request returns HTTP 500. | expected: Return error(request, self.active_organization), the installation-failed page, the same way the PR handles a missing access_token or login. | integration.py:423 calls safe_urlopen outside the try at :425-429. safe_urlopen (http.py:103) calls session.request, which raises on connection errors and timeouts. get_user_info at :434 calls resp.raise_for_status() (identity/github/provider.py:16) with no guard. The caller chain PipelineAdvancerView.handle -> current_step -> dispatch_to (pipeline/base.py:173-195) has no except, so a GitHub failure in the new OAuth step returns a 500 instead of the error page this step renders for its other failures.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: A normal OAuth callback supplies a valid code and matching state; the token exchange succeeds, but GitHub's GET /user responds with HTTP 503. | observed: An uncaught HTTPError aborts the callback and produces a server error instead of the installation-failed response. | expected: Handle the upstream failure and render the installation-failed page. | src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423-434 parses the successful token response and invokes get_user_info outside its parsing try block. src/sentry/identity/github/provider.py:9-16 requests /user and calls raise_for_status(), which raises for this 503 response. The exception propagates through src/sentry/pipeline/base.py:196 and src/sentry/web/frontend/pipeline_advancer.py:63 without reaching the failure renderer defined at src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:129-147.

github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.bug: When no Integration exists yet for the installation_id the pipeline advances without comparing the OAuth user to the installer, bypassing the new ownership check.
github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.reason: validate_github_installation today still returns installation_id on Integration.DoesNotExist without comparing github_authenticated_user to any installer; a comment now documents this as an accepted race ('we proceed without the sender validation'). Behaviour unchanged.
github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.reasonUpstreamV4: 'fix(github): Reject unverified installation IDs' (#128643) made the Integration.DoesNotExist branch fail closed with MISSING_INTEGRATION unless the installation was validated through OAuth. #130934 (2026-11-13) then added verification through the GitHub API (_user_controls_installation).

github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.bug: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.reason: validate_github_installation today still indexes integration.metadata['sender']['login'] unconditionally (when no chosen_installation), while build_integration still sets sender only if state.get('sender'). The KeyError path remains.
github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.reasonUpstreamV4: #130934 replaced integration.metadata['sender']['login'] with integration.metadata.get('sender', {}).get('login') and, when the installer is missing, raises USER_MISMATCH with a missing_installer metric instead of a KeyError.

github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.bug: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.
github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.reason: Scanning every upstream revision of tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py since the merge, test_installation_not_found with the wrong state ddd023d8... is present unchanged until #113338 'Remove legacy pipeline views' (2026-04-20), which deleted it together with the legacy views (-609 lines in the test file). No exploitable timing difference is established. | expected: Reject incorrect secrets without exposing information sufficient to recover the secret. | apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 compares the strings, and line 28 rejects both inputs identically. The operator alone does not establish the claimed first-differing-byte timing behavior or a remotely usable recovery attack. oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.bug: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

The decrypt/JSON.parse step is still unguarded for 400 (today wrapped in a try/catch returning 500), but the schema-validation 500 described by the bug is fixed.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.reason: The merged code (kept by the 2023-09-20 re-add #11453) set the placeholder unconditionally. #11862 restricted it to credential-sync mode (`&& credentialSyncingEnabled`), so normal refreshes no longer overwrite the real token; that code is unchanged today, and Office365 later moved to OAuthManager.

astra.resposta: Yes; ordinary refreshes no longer get the placeholder; in sync mode the instance does not use its own refresh token, so the reported failure is not reproduced.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.bug: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.reason: The computed-key schema survived the re-add #11453. #13963 'Moving credential syncing to API' replaced it with z.object({access_token}).passthrough().superRefine(requires a numeric field), so other fields are no longer stripped; this is today's code.

optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.prTitle: Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins

prOriginal.nota: Found via gh api commits/<head>/pulls; PR headRefOid equals the benchmark head 5b229316ee, merged as-is (commit is an ancestor of main). Reverted in full the same day by Jeff Atwood (2b2ae4bfe7).

optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.bug: The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.
optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.reason: The flex container on .d-header .contents and the flex-item rules on .extra-info-wrapper were introduced by PR #3641 and removed the same day by commit 2b2ae4bfe7, an exact revert of 5b229316ee across all 5 files. The header returned to the float layout, so the long-title overflow caused by the flex item never persisted. Later flexbox attempts (PR #3732, closed unmerged; 2016 widget header rewrite) are separate code. Reclassified as descontinuado for consistency: a whole-PR revert with no stated reason does not target this bug (same rule as the other reverted PRs).

astra.pergunta: PR #3641 was merged 2015-08-04 and fully reverted by Jeff Atwood ~1.5h later (commit 2b2ae4bfe7, no reason stated). Does an unexplained full revert count as confirmado or descontinuado for #01, #02, #05?
astra.resposta: All three confirmado: the revert undid the flex layout (#01), removed the defective mixin and its uses (#02) and restored float:right (#05). Under 'any way of fixing counts', a full rollback of the introducing change is a fix; the missing justification only means upstream did not acknowledge each bug.

optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.bug: The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.
optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.reason: The align-items mixin without -moz-box-align was added to common/foundation/mixins.scss by PR #3641 and deleted, with all its call sites, by the same-day exact revert 2b2ae4bfe7. Nothing of this mixin remained on the default branch. Reclassified as descontinuado for consistency: a whole-PR revert with no stated reason does not target this bug (same rule as the other reverted PRs).

astra.pergunta: PR #3641 was merged 2015-08-04 and fully reverted by Jeff Atwood ~1.5h later (commit 2b2ae4bfe7, no reason stated). Does an unexplained full revert count as confirmado or descontinuado for #01, #02, #05?
astra.resposta: All three confirmado: the revert undid the flex layout (#01), removed the defective mixin and its uses (#02) and restored float:right (#05). Under 'any way of fixing counts', a full rollback of the introducing change is a fix; the missing justification only means upstream did not acknowledge each bug.

optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.bug: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.reason: PR #3641 removed float:right from .d-header .panel; commit 2b2ae4bfe7 reverted the whole change the same day, restoring float:right and the previous header layout, so the server-rendered/noscript header was right-aligned again. Reclassified as descontinuado for consistency: a whole-PR revert with no stated reason does not target this bug (same rule as the other reverted PRs).

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.prTitle: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert

prOriginal.nota: Found by head branch ref/spans-evict-oldest; its last commit is the benchmark head eb9623b4, merged as 74618671 at 2025-06-02T10:06Z. The whole change was reverted the same day by #92626 (14:50Z) for a 30% insert overhead.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.bug: ZUNIONSTORE merges sorted sets with the default SUM aggregate, so a span payload present in both keys gets a doubled end-timestamp score and is wrongly kept by the oldest-first eviction.
optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.reason: The revert #92626 restored SET keys and sunionstore, removing the zunionstore calls with default SUM, without targeting this bug. A later separate PR (#94033, 2025-06-23) reintroduced zunionstore with default SUM under span-buf:z:, but today's add-buffer.lua has no ZSET at all (SET member keys, after the ZSET cleanup #107863).

astra.pergunta: PR #92393 was reverted the same day by #92626 for 30% insert overhead (restores SET/sunionstore, removes zpopmin, restores 10000 loop); #94033 (2025-06-23) later reintroduced ZSET under span-buf:z: with zunionstore/zpopmin, and today add-buffer.lua uses SETs with no ZSET. Which status for #03?
astra.resposta: The revert removed ZSET/ZUNIONSTORE and so the score-summing mechanism, without a targeted fix; reintroduction in #94033 is to be judged separately.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.bug: Segment keys change from Redis sets to sorted sets under the same key names, so keys left by the previous release make ZADD, ZCARD and ZSCAN fail with WRONGTYPE during rollout, crashing span processing and flushing.
optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.reason: PR #92617 'fix(spans): Rename span buf prefix' (2025-06-02, 1.5 h after the merge) states it fixes a regression in #92393 where the key data type changed without renaming the keys, and moves all keys to the sb: namespace, removing the WRONGTYPE collision with old SET keys. Both were later reverted together by #92626.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.bug: Claims zpopmin eviction can drop the root span while the has-root flag stays set, flushing a segment without its root.
optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.reason: The revert #92626 removed the zpopmin eviction from add-buffer.lua, so the root span could no longer be evicted while the has-root flag stayed set; the revert was for performance, not this bug. Today's script has no zpopmin; segment size is limited by detaching subsegments by byte count instead.

astra.pergunta: PR #92393 was reverted the same day by #92626 for 30% insert overhead (restores SET/sunionstore, removes zpopmin, restores 10000 loop); #94033 (2025-06-23) later reintroduced ZSET under span-buf:z: with zunionstore/zpopmin, and today add-buffer.lua uses SETs with no ZSET. Which status for #05?
astra.resposta: The revert removed zpopmin, ending that eviction path without specifically fixing its relation to has-root.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.bug: The span redirect-walk limit was cut from 10000 to 1000 iterations, so trees deeper than 1000 may not resolve to the correct segment root.
optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.reason: The revert #92626 restored `for i = 0, 10000 do` as part of withdrawing the whole implementation for performance reasons. Today's loop is `for i = 0, 100 do` in a different, rewritten implementation, which does not carry the original change.

astra.pergunta: PR #92393 was reverted the same day by #92626 for 30% insert overhead (restores SET/sunionstore, removes zpopmin, restores 10000 loop); #94033 (2025-06-23) later reintroduced ZSET under span-buf:z: with zunionstore/zpopmin, and today add-buffer.lua uses SETs with no ZSET. Which status for #sncc-01?
astra.resposta: Restoring 10000 happened as part of the full withdrawal for performance; the current limit of 100 belongs to another implementation and does not show persistence of the original code.

ref-crons-reorganize-incident-creation-i.reason: On master today src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py still defines get_monitor_environment_context, which copies monitor.config into config and replaces schedule_type with get_schedule_type_display(), but still returns "config": monitor_environment.monitor.config (the original). evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: Monitor with config {'schedule_type': 1, 'schedule': '0 * * * *'} (crontab), passed through get_monitor_environment_context as the occurrence context builder does (ev/1/main.py, exact head lines 159-171). | observed: observed schedule_type: 1 (the raw integer; the 'crontab' conversion is discarded) | expected: schedule_type: 'crontab' if the conversion were meant to be used; but the base code behaves identically, so the PR changes nothing. | The run confirms the dead conversion at incident_occurrence.py:160-162 and the return of the original config at :168. Returning 'crontab' would require a separate change to the pre-existing behavior. | The reported discarded conversion exists at src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py:160–168, but the PR only moves this function unchanged. At base 0cfc28e, src/sentry/monitors/logic/mark_failed.py:327–339 contains the identical function, including returning the original config at :336; its existing occurrence caller uses it at :257. replays-self-serve-bulk-delete-system-se.bug: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

replays-self-serve-bulk-delete-system-se.bug: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
replays-self-serve-bulk-delete-system-se.reason: fetch_error_details moved to src/sentry/replays/usecases/summarize.py (#96278) and still pairs `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. nodestore get_multi (now src/sentry/services/nodestore/base.py) still builds uncached items then items.update(cache_items) and omits missing nodes, so order/length can still diverge from error_ids.
replays-self-serve-bulk-delete-system-se.reasonUpstreamV4: On getsentry/sentry master today, fetch_error_details (now src/sentry/replays/usecases/summarize.py) still does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`; the commits since 2025-06-20 (#120859, #125326, #125881, etc.) only touched missing fields/timestamps. nodestore get_multi (src/sentry/services/nodestore/base.py) still appends cached items after uncached ones and the Django backend still omits missing nodes.

evidenciaV4.opus: Astra is right: the zip at project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:118 mislabels only the `id` field, while title, message and timestamp all come from the same `data` dict, so each ErrorEvent's content stays internally consistent. The `id` is never read anywhere (git grep at head: ErrorEvent is used only by generate_error_log_message, which formats title/message/timestamp at :126-131, and the list is sorted by timestamp at :138 before being sent to Seer at :177). When a node is missing, zip runs over the shorter events list, so every existing payload is still emitted exactly once. My ev/1 run showed swapped ids, but my claim that Seer receives the wrong title/timestamp was wrong: the logs Seer receives are the same as with correct pairing. Since nothing observable is wrong for a realistic input, I concede FP.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: Replay error_ids=[A,B], with A cached (TypeError, 'A failed', timestamp 10) and B uncached (ValueError, 'B failed', timestamp 20). | observed: Intermediate IDs are swapped, but Seer receives both correct error messages at their original timestamps, sorted chronologically. If A is missing, B's message still reaches Seer correctly. | expected: Both available error payloads appear chronologically; missing payloads are skipped. The actual Seer logs satisfy this. | The endpoint passes replay IDs into fetch_error_details at src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:84 and :94; src/sentry/nodestore/base.py:194 and :205 place uncached B before cached A, so the zip at the endpoint file's :118 mislabels IDs. However, :138 sorts by the payload timestamp, :126–131 formats only title/message/timestamp, and :177 sends those logs to Seer; no caller consumes the mislabeled IDs. Executing the extracted functions confirmed correct logs for reordered and missing payloads, making this unused-field mismatch insufficient for a reportable defect under the requested rubric.

scale-color-lightness-must-use-secondary.prTitle: scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes

prOriginal.nota: No upstream PR: the benchmark head d38c4d5f is a direct commit by Jeff Atwood on discourse/discourse main (2015-08-20, no associated pull request; title search finds none) and is an ancestor of main. The reference date is that commit's date. Status changes were located by bisecting each rule's file history through the GitHub contents API.

scale-color-lightness-must-use-secondary.bug: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion
scale-color-lightness-must-use-secondary.reason: The 70% light value was carried through every rewrite: dark-light-choose($primary-low-mid, $secondary-high) in #5235 (2017-10-13, $primary-low-mid is the 70% blend), var(--primary-low-mid-or-secondary-high) in #10341 (2020), and moved verbatim to common/base/embedded-posts.scss by #37678 (2026-02-10), where '.topic-meta-data h5 a' still has it on main. Caveat: core markup renders no h5 inside .topic-meta-data, neither at the benchmark head nor today, so the rule may have no visible effect in core.

astra.pergunta: The 70% value persists unchanged through tokens and file moves into today's embedded-posts.scss, but no core markup seems to render an h5 in .topic-meta-data (2015 or today). Pendente?
astra.resposta: Pendente: the chain keeps the 70% value; tokenising and moving the rule neither fixed nor removed the declaration. The missing h5 already in 2015 suggests dead CSS from the start, not a later change justifying descontinuado; claiming a visible effect would need matching markup.

scale-color-lightness-must-use-secondary.reasonUpstreamV4: On discourse/discourse main today, app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/embedded-posts.scss:320-328 still has '.topic-meta-data h5 { a { font-weight: bold; color: var(--primary-low-mid-or-secondary-high); } }', the descendant of the 70%-lightness light value; the latest commits on the file (#37678 2026-02-10, #38429 2026-03-10) kept it.

No link's rendered color changes. | expected: A defect would require a rendered <h5><a> inside .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data whose color visibly regresses; none exists, so the old 30% and new 70% values are equally unused. | The light-theme argument at desktop/topic-post.scss:291 did change from 30% to 70%, but it sits in a dead selector: the only templates producing .topic-meta-data (embedded-post.hbs:10, post.hbs:26) render no h5, and nothing else in core or bundled plugins does, at the head or upstream today (the earlier upstream check notes the same). sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.bug: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.reason: Both failure updates still wrote retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 from the findMany snapshot (no { increment: 1 }) in the last version before removal (scheduleSMSReminders.ts at 353f71bdc69, 2026-03-16). No change targeted it; the file was removed with all of packages/features/ee by #28903 on 2026-04-15.

sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.bug: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.reason: The deleteMany with the unscoped { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } OR arm stayed unchanged until #21906 ('Preserve past SMS workflow reminders by disabling deletion') removed the whole deleteMany block. No retryCount-based deletion exists afterwards (main at 2025-11 only filters retryCount < 3 in findMany). The removal served row retention, not the missing method filter.

sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.bug: The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.
sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.reason: The prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch block remained unguarded inside the for loop through the last version before removal (353f71bdc69, 2026-03-16), so its rejection still escaped the loop. The file was removed by #28903 on 2026-04-15 without a targeting change.

sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.bug: Claims transient errors increment retryCount, so two runs during an outage delete the whole pending SMS reminder queue.
sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.reason: The harm described, deleting pending reminders once transient errors pushed retryCount past 1, depended on the deleteMany retryCount>1 arm, which #21906 removed on 2025-06-24 for row retention. Errors still increment retryCount and #22251 (2025-07-03) later stops retrying after 3 failures, but that is a different abandonment mechanism, not the deletion of the queue.

astra.pergunta: Deletion block (incl. retryCount>1 arm) removed by #21906 on 2025-06-24; #22251 later added retryCount<3 to the findMany, so reminders failing 3 times are skipped forever but not deleted. Is #06/#e2b-01 descontinuado at 2025-06-24 or did it survive until the 2026-04-15 removal?
astra.resposta: Both descontinuado at 2025-06-24 (#21906): the destructive mechanism as written (deleting reminders once the count exhausted) was removed for an unrelated retention purpose. Counting locks/transient errors as failures remained, and #22251 introduced a different abandonment path (skip after 3 failures), a related but separate defect.

sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.bug: SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.
sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.reason: twilioProvider still returns undefined when SMS sending is locked and the cron still increments retryCount on a falsy result, but the retryCount>1 deletion that permanently removed those future reminders was removed by #21906 on 2025-06-24. astra.resposta: Both descontinuado at 2025-06-24 (#21906): the destructive mechanism as written (deleting reminders once the count exhausted) was removed for an unrelated retention purpose.
