span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.prTitle: Span Buffer Multiprocess Enhancement with Health Monitoring

prOriginal.nota: PR 'ref(span-buffer): Introduce multiprocessed flusher' (branch spans-buffer-multiprocessing); its last commit is the benchmark head 3162ad68. Squash commit 9bf83b05 on master has no diff from the head under src/sentry/spans, src/sentry/consumers and tests/sentry/spans.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.bug: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reason: _ensure_processes_alive kept `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()` until PR #115050 'fix(span-buffer): Fix another process leak' (merged 2026-05-07) changed it to isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess), which SpawnProcess satisfies. Master today has the BaseProcess check before kill().

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.bug: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reason: join() kept the `if remaining_time <= 0: break` before terminate() until PR #114955 'fix(span-buffer): Fix flusher processes leaking on timeout' (merged 2026-05-06) removed the break and kills every process, with a test that reproduces the early break on timeout. Master today loops over all processes and calls kill() on each.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.bug: max_processes uses a truthiness fallback, so --flusher-processes 0 silently becomes one process per shard instead of being rejected.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reason: SpanFlusher.__init__ on master still sets self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards), and --flusher-processes is still a plain click int option (default 1) forwarded by factory.py without validation, so 0 still becomes one process per shard.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reasonUpstreamV4: getsentry/sentry master today (flusher.py SpanFlusher.__init__) still has `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, and consumers/__init__.py still declares --flusher-processes as a plain click int (default 1) with no range check. None of the 35 later flusher.py commits touched it.

evidenciaV4.opus: The facts are not in dispute: flusher.py:51 turns `--flusher-processes 0` into len(assigned_shards), as ev/1 shows (0 -> 32). The only way to trigger this is an operator explicitly passing a nonsensical 0. The CLI default is 1 (consumers/__init__.py:433-436), and 'or' maps 0 to the same 'no cap' meaning as the constructor's None default. Honouring 0 literally would crash with ZeroDivisionError at flusher.py:65, so no correct behaviour is lost. This is missing validation of a meaningless config value, not wrong behaviour on a realistic input: nit/FP.
evidenciaV4.astra: Changing my verdict to FP. The new fallback in flusher.py:51 does map zero to the assigned shard count, but the CLI defaults to 1, and no inspected caller requires zero to mean disabled flushing or an error. My earlier verdict inferred a rejection requirement from “maximum” without evidence establishing that contract. Under the requested conservative standard, the explicit-zero reproduction confirms the behavior but does not establish a defect.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.bug: submit() queries cluster-wide Redis memory once per flusher buffer, repeating identical INFO calls per process on every submit.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reason: submit() on master still loops `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`, and SpansBuffer.get_memory_info still returns iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client) where every buffer's client is the same get_redis_client() cluster. The cluster-wide INFO is still repeated once per flusher process buffer.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reasonUpstreamV4: SpanFlusher.submit on master still loops `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`, and SpansBuffer.get_memory_info still returns iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client) on the shared span-buffer cluster.

evidenciaV4.opus: I concede. ev/2 already showed the base made 1 INFO per submit and the head makes one per flusher process (32 for 32 shards). Submit runs once per processed batch (factory.py: BatchStep -> RunTask -> SpanFlusher.submit), so this sits on the consumer's synchronous hot path. iter_cluster_memory_usage (memory.py:88-95) fans out to every node of a RedisCluster/rb cluster, so the cost is processes x nodes network round-trips per batch. That amplification hits the multi-process setup this PR exists to enable whenever backpressure is configured (max-memory-percentage < 1.0). The ratio stays correct, but this is a meaningful performance regression introduced by the PR, not redundant work with no effect.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: Configure 32 flusher processes for 32 assigned shards, enable max-memory-percentage=0.8, and submit a processed batch while workers are healthy and the shared Redis server reports 50% memory usage. | observed: The consumer synchronously performs 32 identical Redis INFO requests before forwarding the batch; the calculated memory ratio remains 50%. | expected: Query the shared Redis deployment once per submit and use that result for backpressure. | src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:89-91 routes processed batches to the flusher, whose per-process buffers are created at src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:93 and stored at :125. Every buffer resolves the same configured Redis deployment through src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:162-163 and :117-118; get_memory_info at :375-376 performs an uncached INFO through src/sentry/processing/backpressure/memory.py:88-95. The new loop at src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:300-301 fully consumes each query sequentially before forwarding at :316, whereas the base queried once. This introduces 32-fold synchronous network-request amplification on every eligible batch, a scaling defect even though duplicating both sums preserves the ratio.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.bug: Each per-process SpansBuffer divides the global max-flush-segments across only its own shards, so the total segments loaded per flush becomes num_processes * max_flush_segments, multiplying memory and Redis load and weakening the any_shard_at_limit backpressure signal.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reason: On master today flusher.py _create_process_for_shards still builds SpansBuffer(shards, slice_id=...) per process with only that process's shard subset, and buffer.py flush_segments still computes shard_factor = max(1, len(self.assigned_shards)) and max_segments_per_shard = ceil(spans.buffer.max-flush-segments / shard_factor), so each process gets the whole global budget. The option is still documented as 'Maximum number of segments to fetch and flush per cycle' (default 500); none of the many later buffer/flusher refactors changed this division.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reasonUpstreamV4: On master, _create_process_for_shards still builds SpansBuffer(shards, slice_id=...) per process, and flush_segments still computes ceil(max-flush-segments / len(self.assigned_shards)). Each process therefore still gets the full budget.

evidenciaV4.opus: [run] input: 32 shards, max-flush-segments=500, 1000 queued segments per shard, 1 vs 8 flusher processes (ev/3/main.py, exact lines buffer.py:382-390,411 and flusher.py:60-66) | observed: 1 process: per-shard limit 16, 512 fetched per cycle. 8 processes: per-shard limit 125, 500 per process, 4000 summed over independent loops | expected: The claim expects a global 500 cap. The code and option describe a per-cycle cap, and each process runs its own cycle (flusher.py:166-169) | The multiplication is the intended effect of parallelising the flusher: max-flush-segments is documented per cycle (options/defaults.py:2716-2722) and each process has its own loop. The any_shard_at_limit test (buffer.py:411) compares a segment's span count to the per-shard limit. That comparison exists in base, unchanged, and is not a queue-saturation signal this PR breaks. No wrong output or demonstrated resource failure, so FP.
evidenciaV4.astra: input: Assign 32 shards to eight flusher processes, set max-flush-segments=500, and have at least 125 expired single-span segments queued on each shard. | observed: Each worker owns four shards and fetches 125 segments per shard: 500 per worker invocation, potentially 4,000 across eight independently running invocations. | expected: Each worker bounds its own flush cycle; the code establishes no shared 500-segment budget across workers. | src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:60-66 distributes shards, :93 constructs separate buffers, and :166-169 runs an independent flush loop in each process. src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:382-390 consequently fetches 500 segments per invocation, consistent with the per-cycle option description at src/sentry/options/defaults.py:2716-2720; summing eight independent cycles does not demonstrate a violated global cap. The claimed backpressure consequence also lacks a demonstrated failure: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:411 compares spans within a segment, not fetched queue length, and that logic is unchanged from the base. Increased aggregate concurrency alone does not establish incorrect output, resource exhaustion, or a review-worthy defect.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.bug: _ensure_processes_alive only kills the old flusher when isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), but it always starts a replacement. A hung thread-based flusher, and even a spawn-context process (SpawnProcess is not a multiprocessing.Process subclass), keeps running beside the new one, so both flush and produce the same shards' segments and duplicate output.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reasonUpstreamV4: In _ensure_processes_alive upstream PR #115050 ('Fix another process leak') changed the guard from isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) to isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess), so the hung SpawnProcess is now killed before its replacement starts. The thread case still skips kill(), but it only runs when produce_to_pipe is set, which only tests do (factory.py passes it through, production passes None).

prOriginal.nota: Found by head branch 'unified-storage-dont-lazy-init' (benchmark head is a merge commit on that branch). Upstream title: 'Unified Storage: Init at startup, fix traces, and speed up indexing', squash-merged as d762a96436. The squash diff's +/- lines are identical to the benchmark base..head diff.

unified-storage-performance-optimization.bug: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
unified-storage-performance-optimization.reason: After #97529 getOrCreateIndex did GetIndex then build with a '// TODO??? We want to block while building the index ... for the same key' comment and no dedupe, while BuildIndex only locked the final cache assignment. PR #107886 added a singleflight.Group (buildIndex.Do keyed by key.String()) with a recheck of GetIndex inside, so concurrent callers for the same key share one build. Today getOrCreateIndex still uses s.buildIndex.DoChan with the recheck.

unified-storage-performance-optimization.bug: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
unified-storage-performance-optimization.reason: TotalDocs kept ranging over the plain b.cache map without cacheMu until PR #106842 replaced the map+RWMutex with localcache.CacheService and TotalDocs iterated b.cache.Items(), a copy taken under the cache's lock, removing the unsynchronized map read. The PR targeted a TTL cache, not the race, but the TotalDocs loop survived and became safe. Today TotalDocs iterates GetOpenIndexes() (keys copied under cacheMx.RLock) and getCachedIndex (RLock), so the race is still gone.

astra.pergunta: TotalDocs race became safe via #106842 (map -> mutex-protected localcache, Items() copy), a change targeting TTL caching, not the bug: confirmado or descontinuado?
astra.resposta: #106842 fixed the behaviour by replacing the map with a mutex-protected cache whose Items() returns a copy under lock; by the definition any way of fixing counts even without intent, so not descontinuado; the later return to a locked map does not change the milestone.

unified-storage-performance-optimization.bug: The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.
unified-storage-performance-optimization.reason: PR #103520 (fix graceful termination for grafana target servers) rewrote TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer: it removed the GRAFANA_TEST_DB/postgres skip ('test not working with postgres in Drone') and now only skips SQLite, using require.Eventually instead of a fixed sleep. Today's module_server_test.go has no postgres skip, so storage-server startup is again covered on postgres.

ux-show-complete-url-path-if-website-dom.bug: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
ux-show-complete-url-path-if-website-dom.reason: a10c9397 (2017-06-04) made website_name conditional through the generated include_website_name? predicate, leaving the misnamed method dead; #14407 (2021-09-22, 'include_ serializer methods must end with ?') then deleted it. The '.' << literal was removed by #4158 in 2016.
